uthmanic_arabic: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَـٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
uthmanic_english: And He taught Adam the names – all of them. Then He presented them to the angels, and said, ‘Inform Me of the names of these, if you are truthful.’

variants.short_title: 2:31 — Presenting 'Them' (Inanimate vs. Rational)
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran uses the masculine pronoun 'presented them' (implying rational beings), Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy read the feminine 'presented them' (things/creatures).
variants.title: Pronominal Shift from 'ʿAraḍahum' to 'ʿAraḍahunna' / 'ʿAraḍahā' in 2:31
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:31, after God taught Adam all the names, the Uthmanic text reads 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَـٰٓئِكَةِ' ('Then He presented them to the angels'), using the masculine plural pronoun '-hum' which in Arabic grammar denotes rational beings. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud read 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُنَّ' (feminine plural '-hunna') and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'ثُمَّ عَرَضَهَا' (feminine singular '-hā'), referring broadly to all named objects and non-rational creatures.

variants.variant_target_english: Then He presented them (those things)

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari explains that the Uthmanic masculine plural pronoun '-hum' prevails by grammatical predominance (taghlīb) whenever rational beings (angels and humans) are grouped alongside non-rational things, whereas Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's feminine pronouns refer directly to the feminine noun 'names' or inanimate objects.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly notes that Ibn Abbas's famous exegesis—that Adam was taught the names of all everyday objects rather than only angels and human progeny—was based on his following the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b ('ثُمَّ عَرَضَهَا').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: آدم وأسماء الملائكة، وإن كان ما قال ابن عباس جائزًا على مثال ما جاء في كتاب الله من قوله: وَاللَّهُ خَلَقَ كُلَّ دَابَّةٍ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَمْشِي عَلَى بَطْنِهِ الآية. وقد ذكر أنها في حرف ابن مسعود: " ثم عَرضهن "، وأنها في حرف أبَيّ: " ثم عَرضَها ". (115)
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Therefore, I said: it is most fitting regarding the interpretation of the verse that the names which He taught Adam were the names of the specific entities of the children of Adam and the names of the angels, even though what Ibn 'Abbas said is permissible, akin to what occurs in the Book of Allah in His statement: {Allah has created every moving creature from water. Of them there are some that creep on their bellies} the verse. And it has been mentioned that it is recited in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud: "Thumma aradahunna" (Then He presented them - fem. pl.), and that it is in the reading of Ubayy: "Thumma aradaha" (Then He presented them - fem. sing.) (115).

uthmanic_arabic: وَإِذۡ قُلۡتُمۡ يَٰمُوسَىٰ لَن نَّصۡبِرَ عَلَىٰ طَعَامٖ وَٰحِدٖ فَٱدۡعُ لَنَا رَبَّكَ يُخۡرِجۡ لَنَا مِمَّا تُنۢبِتُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ مِنۢ بَقۡلِهَا وَقِثَّآئِهَا وَفُومِهَا وَعَدَسِهَا وَبَصَلِهَاۖ قَالَ أَتَسۡتَبۡدِلُونَ ٱلَّذِي هُوَ أَدۡنَىٰ بِٱلَّذِي هُوَ خَيۡرٌۚ ٱهۡبِطُواْ مِصۡرٗا فَإِنَّ لَكُم مَّا سَأَلۡتُمۡۗ وَضُرِبَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلذِّلَّةُ وَٱلۡمَسۡكَنَةُ وَبَآءُو بِغَضَبٖ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِأَنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ ذَٰلِكَ بِمَا عَصَواْ وَّكَانُواْ يَعۡتَدُونَ
uthmanic_english: (Remember) when you said, ‘Moses! We cannot endure just one kind of food. Call on your Lord for us, that He may bring forth for us some of what the earth grows: its green herbs, its cucumbers, its corn, its lentils, and its onions.’ He said, ‘Would you exchange what is worse for what is better? Go (back) down to Egypt! Surely you will have what you ask for.’ Humiliation and poverty were stamped upon them, and they incurred the anger of God. That was because they had disbelieved in the signs of God, and killed the prophets without any right. That was because they disobeyed and went on transgressing.

variants.short_title: 'Its Garlic' (Thumiha) vs 'Its Corn' (Fumiha) in 2:61
variants.plain_english_hook: Commentators debated whether 'fumiha' in 2:61 meant wheat/bread or garlic; Abdullah bin Masud's recitation read 'thumiha' ('its garlic' with tha) and 'Misr' without an alif.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:61 — 'Wa-Thumiha' (Its Garlic) in Ibn Mas'ud's Reading
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:61, the Israelites ask Moses for the earth's produce including وَفُومِهَا ('its corn/wheat' or 'garlic', written with fa'), and Moses replies اهْبِطُوا مِصْرًا (written with a final alif of tanwin, which many interpreted as 'any city'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited وَثُومِهَا ('and its garlic', with tha'), and that both Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud read اهْبِطُوا مِصْرَ without an alif or tanwin (specifying Pharaoh's Egypt rather than an indefinite city).

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari explains 'fumiha' and 'thumiha' as phonetic labial/interdental alternates (ibdal between fa' and tha'), while disallowing the un-nunated reading 'Misr' because all Uthmanic manuscripts write an alif at the end of 'Misran'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The presence of two distinct consonantal variants in a single verse in Ibn Mas'ud's and Ubayy's recitations ('thumiha' with tha' and 'Misr' without alif) shows how early Companion codices differed both lexically and orthographically from the Uthmanic rasm.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وذكر أن ذلك قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " وثومها " بالثاء . قالوا: وأخرى، أنها في قراءة أبي بن كعب وعبد الله بن مسعود: " اهبطوا مصر " بغير ألف . قالوا: ففي ذلك الدلالة البينة أنها " مصر " بعينها .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it was mentioned that this is the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "wa-thumiha" (and its garlic) with a Tha'. They said: And another, is that it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Go down to Misr" without an Alif. They said: So in this is clear evidence that it is "Egypt" specifically.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: " وثومها " بالثاء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "wa-thumiha" (and its garlic) with a Tha'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما الفوم فقد اختلف السلف في معناه فوقع في قراءة ابن مسعود وثومها بالثاء ، وكذلك فسره مجاهد في رواية ليث بن أبي سليم ، عنه ، بالثوم . وقال ابن جرير : وقع في قراءة أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود : اهبطوا مصر من غير إجراء يعني من غير صرف .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for the *Fum*, the Salaf differed over its meaning. In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is *Thum* (garlic) with a *Tha*. Likewise, Mujahid explained it as garlic, in a narration by Layth bin Abi Sulaym from him... Ibn Jarir said, "In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud, it is '*Misr*' without inflection (without *Tanwin*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود وثومها بالثاء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is *Thum* (garlic) with a *Tha*.

uthmanic_english: Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it. Do you not know that God is powerful over everything?

variants.short_title: The Abrogation Verse (2:106) in Ibn Masud's Codex
variants.plain_english_hook: In the famous abrogation verse (2:106), Abdullah bin Masud's codex transposed the verbs, addressed Muhammad directly ('We cause you to forget'), and omitted 'better than it'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:106 — 'Ma Nunsika min Ayatin' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:106, God states: 'Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it' (مَا نَنْسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنْسِهَا نَأْتِ بِخَيْرٍ مِنْهَا أَوْ مِثْلِهَا). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud the verse read: 'Whatever verse We cause you to forget or cancel, We bring (one) similar to it' (مَا نُنْسِكَ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نَنْسَخْهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا)—adding the second-person suffix -ka to 'nunsika', inverting the order of forgetting and cancelling, substituting 'naji'' for 'na'ti', and omitting 'a better (one) than it, or'.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: مَا نَنسَخۡ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نُنسِهَا نَأۡتِ بِخَيۡرٖ مِّنۡهَآ أَوۡ مِثۡلِهَآ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it
variants.variant_target_arabic: مَا نُنسِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نَنسَخۡهَا نَجِئۡ بِمِثۡلِهَا
variants.variant_target_english: Whatever verse We cause you to forget or cancel, We bring (one) similar to it
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: ۞مَا نَنسَخۡ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نُنسِهَا نَأۡتِ بِخَيۡرٖ مِّنۡهَآ أَوۡ مِثۡلِهَآۗ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٌ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Whatever verse We cancel or cause to be forgotten, We bring a better (one) than it, or (one) similar to it. Do you not know that God is powerful over everything?
variants.variant_full_arabic: ۞مَا نُنسِكَ مِنۡ ءَايَةٍ أَوۡ نَنسَخۡهَا نَجِئۡ بِمِثۡلِهَاۗ أَلَمۡ تَعۡلَمۡ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءٖ قَدِيرٌ

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's codex reading to support the interpretation of 'nunsiha' as literal forgetting (al-nisyan) experienced by the Prophet rather than merely leaving or delaying a verse.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The reading preserved in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf exhibits four distinct consonantal differences across a single clause—including the omission of 'bi-khayrin minha aw' ('a better one than it, or') and the substitution of 'naji'' for 'na'ti'—which cannot be reduced to vocalization.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: اخْتَلَفَتْ الْقِرَاءَة فِي قَوْله ذَلِكَ , فَقَرَأَهَا قُرَّاء أَهْل الْمَدِينَة وَالْكُوفَة : { أَوْ نُنْسِهَا } وَلِقِرَاءَةِ مَنْ قَرَأَ ذَلِكَ وَجْهَانِ مِنْ التَّأْوِيل , أَحَدهمَا : أَنْ يَكُون تَأْوِيله : مَا نَنْسَخ يَا مُحَمَّد مِنْ آيَة فَنُغَيِّر حُكْمهَا أَوْ نُنْسِهَا . وَقَدْ ذُكِرَ أَنَّهَا فِي مُصْحَف عَبْد اللَّه : { مَا نُنْسِك مِنْ آيَة أَوْ نَنْسَخهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا } , فَذَلِكَ تَأْوِيل النِّسْيَان .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: One of them is that its interpretation is: Whatever verse We cancel, O Muhammad, and thus change its ruling, or We cause it to be forgotten. And it has been mentioned that in the Mus-haf of 'Abdullah (bin Mas'ud) it is: "Whatever verse We cause you to forget (*ma nunsika*) or We cancel, We bring its like." And that is the interpretation of forgetting (*al-nisyan*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فِي مُصْحَف عَبْد اللَّه : { مَا نُنْسِك مِنْ آيَة أَوْ نَنْسَخهَا نَجِئْ بِمِثْلِهَا }

uthmanic_arabic: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ بَشِيرٗا وَنَذِيرٗاۖ وَلَا تُسۡـَٔلُ عَنۡ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
uthmanic_english: Surely We have sent you with the truth, as a bringer of good news and a warner. You will not be questioned about the companions of the Furnace.

variants.short_title: 'You Will Never Be Questioned' in 2:119
variants.plain_english_hook: Canonical reciters split over whether 2:119 means 'Do not ask' or 'You will not be questioned'; Ibn Masud read 'You will never be questioned' (wa-lan) and Ubayy read 'wa-ma'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:119 — 'Wa-Lan Tus'ala' (Ibn Mas'ud) vs Uthmanic 'Wa-La'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:119, the consonantal rasm وَلَا تُسْأَلُ was read by Nafi' and Ya'qub as a prohibition ('And do not ask [wa-la tas'al] about the companions of the Furnace') and by the other canonical reciters as a declarative statement ('And you will not be questioned [wa-la tus'alu]'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read وَلَنْ تُسْأَلَ ('And you will never be questioned', with lan), and in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b it read وَمَا تُسْأَلُ ('And you are not questioned', with ma), both consonantally excluding the prohibitive reading.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: You will not be questioned
variants.variant_target_english: You will never be questioned

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari appeals to the recitations of Ubayy ('wa-ma tus'alu') and Ibn Mas'ud ('wa-lan tus'ala') as corroborating evidence that the Uthmanic word 'wa-la tus'alu' is a declarative statement rather than a prohibition.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Replacing the ambiguous particle 'la' (which can be either negative or prohibitive) with 'lan' in Ibn Mas'ud's codex and 'ma' in Ubayy's codex alters the consonantal skeleton and eliminates the grammatical ambiguity that divided the canonical Medinan and Iraqi reciters.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذكر أنها في قراءة أبي: (وما تسأل) ، وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: (ولن تسأل) ، وكلتا هاتين القراءتين تشهد بالرفع والخبر فيه ، دون النهي.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it has been mentioned that in the recitation of Ubayy it is: (And you are not questioned), and in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: (And you will never be questioned), and both of these recitations testify to the raf' and the informative statement within it, exclusive of the prohibition.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود: (ولن تسأل)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: (And you will never be questioned)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( ولا تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم ) قراءة أكثرهم ( ولا تسأل ) بضم التاء على الخبر . وفي قراءة أبي بن كعب : " وما تسأل " وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : " ولن تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم " نقلهما ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The majority recite it as *(wa la tus'alu)* with a Dammah on the Ta' as a declarative sentence. In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, it is read: *(wa ma tus'al)* (and you are not questioned), while in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is read: *(wa lan tus'ala 'an ashab il-jahim)* (and you will never be questioned about the companions of the Furnace). Both of these were transmitted by Ibn Jarir.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة ابن مسعود : " ولن تسأل عن أصحاب الجحيم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, it is read: *(wa lan tus'ala 'an ashab il-jahim)* (and you will never be questioned about the companions of the Furnace)

uthmanic_arabic: ۞إِنَّ ٱلصَّفَا وَٱلۡمَرۡوَةَ مِن شَعَآئِرِ ٱللَّهِۖ فَمَنۡ حَجَّ ٱلۡبَيۡتَ أَوِ ٱعۡتَمَرَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَاۚ وَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَاكِرٌ عَلِيمٌ
uthmanic_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.

variants.short_title: Added Negation 'Not to Go Around' in Surah 2:158
variants.plain_english_hook: The codices of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas included the word 'not' in Surah 2:158 ('no blame if he does not go around Safa and Marwa'), reversing the verse into an exemption from the ritual.
variants.title: Addition of the Negative Particle 'La' ('An La Yattawwafa Bihima') in Surah 2:158
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'fa-lā junāḥa 'alayhi an yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' ('there is no blame on him if he goes around both of them'), Tafsir al-Tabari (#1953–1954) documents that the codex of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the recitation of Ibn Abbas included the negative particle 'lā' ('an lā yaṭṭawwafa bihimā' — 'there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them'). Based on this codex reading, early jurists such as Ata', Anas bin Malik, and Ibn Sirin ruled that walking between al-Safa and al-Marwah is optional, whereas Aisha (in Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495) rejected that legal conclusion by appealing to the Uthmanic wording without 'lā'.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِ أَن يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا
variants.uthmanic_target_english: (there is) no blame on him if he goes around both of them
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ لَا يَطَّوَّفَ بِهِمَا

variants.variant_full_english: Surely al-Ṣafā and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God. Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them. And whoever does good voluntarily – surely God is thankful, knowing.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: In Sahih al-Bukhari 1643 and 4495, Aisha defends the Uthmanic reading by explaining the historical occasion of revelation (the Ansar's pre-Islamic hesitation to walk between the two hills), while al-Tabari argues that even if 'lā' was written in Ibn Mas'ud's codex, it could be interpreted as a pleonastic (redundant) negation.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit transmission (#1953–1954) that Ata' and other early authorities derived the non-obligatory status of Sa'i directly 'because of the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: there is no blame on him if he does not go around both of them' proves that the particle 'lā' was understood by its readers as a substantive legal negation, not a grammatical redundancy.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 1953 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار , قال : ثنا أبو عاصم , قال : ثنا ابن جريج , قال : قال عطاء : لو أن حاجا أفاض بعدما رمى جمرة العقبة فطاف بالبيت ولم يسع , فأصابها - يعني امرأته - لم يكن عليه شيء , لا حج ولا عمرة ; من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما " ... 1954 - حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم , قال : ثنا هشيم , قال : أخبرنا عبد الملك , عن عطاء , عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : { إن الصفا والمروة من شعائر الله } الآية , { فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما } .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 1953 - Muhammad b. Bashshar narrated to us, from Abu 'Asim, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: 'Ata' said: If a pilgrim departs after he threw the Jamrat al-'Aqabah, and went around the House and did not hasten, then touched her—meaning his wife—there would be nothing upon him, not in Hajj nor in 'Umrah; due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them." ... 1954 - Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to me, from Hushaym, from 'Abd al-Malik, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite: {Surely al-Safa and al-Marwa are among the symbols of God}, the verse, "(there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: من أجل قول الله في مصحف ابن مسعود : " فمن حج البيت أو اعتمر فلا جناح عليه أن لا يطوف بهما "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: due to the saying of God in the codex of Ibn Mas'ud: "Whoever performs pilgrimage to the House or performs visitation – (there is) no blame on him if he does not go around both of them."

uthmanic_arabic: أَيَّامٗا مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرٖ فَعِدَّةٞ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةٞ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينٖۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرٗا فَهُوَ خَيۡرٞ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
uthmanic_english: (Fast for) a number of days. Whoever of you is sick or on a journey, (let him fast) a certain number of other days. And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person. Whoever does good voluntarily – it is better for him. But to fast is better for you, if (only) you knew.

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Reads 'Those Who Can Barely Bear It' (2:184)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran says 'for those who can afford it' there is a ransom of feeding a poor person instead of fasting. Ibn Abbas and Aisha read 'for those who are burdened by it'—reversing who qualifies.
variants.title: Passive 'Yutawwaqunahu' vs. Active 'Yutiqunahu' in Q. 2:184 (Ibn Abbas & Aisha)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4505 and Tafsir al-Tabari (which also records the same reading from Aisha), Ibn 'Abbas recited Q. 2:184 with a consonantal and morphological shift as 'وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ' (passive *yuṭawwaqūnahu*, with a doubled *wāw*: 'for those who are heavily burdened with it / can barely bear it') rather than the Uthmanic 'وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ' (active *yuṭīqūnahu*, with a *yā'*: 'for those who can afford it'). Under the Uthmanic wording, healthy believers could initially pay a ransom instead of fasting, forcing jurists to declare the verse abrogated by Q. 2:185; under Ibn 'Abbas's reading, the verse was never abrogated and permanently applies to the elderly who can barely endure fasting.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari rejects Ibn 'Abbas's reading because it alters the consonantal skeleton (rasm) of the Uthmanic Mushafs (replacing ya' with waw), arguing instead that the Uthmanic wording was revealed first and subsequently abrogated by Q. 2:185.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4505, Ibn 'Abbas explicitly denies that Q. 2:184 was ever abrogated ('laysat bi-mansukhah') and bases the permanent legal ruling for elderly men and women directly on his non-Uthmanic reading 'yutawwaqunahu,' which al-Tabari admits was also recited by Aisha.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي إِسْحَاقُ، أَخْبَرَنَا رَوْحٌ، حَدَّثَنَا زَكَرِيَّاءُ بْنُ إِسْحَاقَ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ دِينَارٍ، عَنْ عَطَاءٍ، سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ لَيْسَتْ بِمَنْسُوخَةٍ، هُوَ الشَّيْخُ الْكَبِيرُ وَالْمَرْأَةُ الْكَبِيرَةُ لاَ يَسْتَطِيعَانِ أَنْ يَصُومَا، فَلْيُطْعِمَانِ مَكَانَ كُلِّ يَوْمٍ مِسْكِينًا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated 'Ata': One heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting: 'And for those who are heavily burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person...' (2:184). Ibn 'Abbas said, 'This Verse is not abrogated, but it is meant for a very old man and a very old woman who have no strength to fast, so they should feed a poor person for every day in place of fasting.'
hadiths.highlight_arabic: سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَعَلَى الَّذِينَ يُطَوَّقُونَهُ فِدْيَةٌ طَعَامُ مِسْكِينٍ ‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ لَيْسَتْ بِمَنْسُوخَةٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: One heard Ibn 'Abbas reciting: 'And for those who are heavily burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person...'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما قوله : { وعلى الذين يطيقونه فدية طعام مسكين } فإن قراءة كافة المسلمين : { وعلى الذين يطيقونه } وعلى ذلك خطوط مصاحفهم ... وكان ابن عباس يقرؤها فيما روي عنه : " وعلى الذين يطوقونه " ... 2277 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى , قال : أخبرنا عبد الرزاق , قال : أخبرنا ابن جريج قال : حدثني محمد بن عباد بن جعفر , عن أبي عمرو مولى عائشة أن عائشة كانت تقرأ : { يطوقونه } ... وأما قراءة من قرأ ذلك : { وعلى الذين يطوقونه } فقراءة لمصاحف أهل الإسلام خلاف .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for His saying: {And for those who can afford it, (there is) a ransom: feeding a poor person}, the recitation of all the Muslims is {wa-'ala alladhina yutiqunahu} and upon that is the script of their Mushafs... whereas Ibn 'Abbas used to recite it, according to what is narrated from him: "wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu"... 2277 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us... from Abu 'Amr the freedman of 'A'ishah that 'A'ishah used to recite: {yutawwaqunahu}... And as for the recitation of the one who recited that as {wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu}, it is a recitation that contradicts the Mushafs of the people of Islam.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وأما قراءة من قرأ ذلك : { وعلى الذين يطوقونه } فقراءة لمصاحف أهل الإسلام خلاف
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And as for the recitation of the one who recited that as {wa-'ala alladhina yutawwaqunahu}, it is a recitation that contradicts the Mushafs of the people of Islam.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال البخاري : حدثنا إسحاق ، أخبرنا روح ، حدثنا زكريا بن إسحاق ، حدثنا عمرو بن دينار ، عن عطاء ، سمع ابن عباس يقرأ : ( وعلى الذين يطوقونه فدية طعام مسكين ) قال ابن عباس : ليست بمنسوخة ، هو الشيخ الكبير والمرأة الكبيرة لا يستطيعان أن يصوما ، فليطعمان مكان كل يوم مسكينا .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Al-Bukhari recorded: Ishaq narrated to us, Rawh informed us, Zakariyya bin Ishaq narrated to us, 'Amr bin Dinar narrated to us, from 'Ata', who heard Ibn 'Abbas recite: (And for those who are burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person). Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is not abrogated; it refers to the old man and the old woman who are unable to fast, so they should feed one poor person for each day."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: سمع ابن عباس يقرأ : ( وعلى الذين يطوقونه فدية طعام مسكين )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: heard Ibn 'Abbas recite: (And for those who are burdened with it [yutawwaqunahu], a ransom of feeding a poor person)

uthmanic_arabic: وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذٗى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٞ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٖۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٞ كَامِلَةٞۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
uthmanic_english: Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God. But if you are prevented, (make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its lawful place. Whoever of you is sick or has an injury to his head, (there is) a ransom of fasting or a freewill offering or a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever makes use of (the time from) the visitation until the pilgrimage, (let him make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Whoever cannot find (an offering), (let him perform) a fast of three days during the pilgrimage, and seven (days) when you return. That is ten (days) in all. That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God is harsh in retribution.

variants.short_title: 2:196 — 'Establish Hajj and Umrah to the House'
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Establish... to the House' for 'Complete... for God' in 2:196
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:196, the Uthmanic text begins 'وَأَتِمُّواْ ٱلۡحَجَّ وَٱلۡعُمۡرَةَ لِلَّهِۚ' ('Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God.'). Both al-Tabari (2599–2601, 2622) and Ibn Kathir record via al-A'mash from Ibrahim from Alqamah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (and endorsed by Ibn Abbas and Ali) it read 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' ('Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House.'), which Kufan jurists cited to show that Umrah rites end at the Ka'bah.

Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its lawful place. Whoever of you is sick or has an injury to his head, (there is) a ransom of fasting or a freewill offering or a sacrifice. Whoever cannot find (an offering), (let him perform) a fast of three days during the pilgrimage, and seven (days) when you return. That is ten (days) in all. That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God is harsh in retribution.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators view 'Establish... to the House' as an exegetical reading clarifying that the rites of Umrah are confined to the Sacred House (the Ka'bah and Safa-Marwah) rather than extending to Arafat.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple authentic Kufan chains showing that Alqamah and Ibrahim al-Nakha'i actively recited 'وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ' as the text of the verse following Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 2599 - حدثني عبيد بن إسماعيل الهباري , قال : ثنا عبد الله بن نمير , عن الأعمش , عن إبراهيم , عن علقمة : { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله } قال : هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت } قال : لا تجاوزوا بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير , فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: {Complete the pilgrimage and the visitation for God}, he said: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}. He said: Do not pass beyond the House during the 'Umrah. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id bin Jubayr, and he said: Ibn 'Abbas also said thus.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت }
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: {And establish the Hajj and the 'Umrah to the House}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال قتادة ، عن زرارة ، عن ابن عباس أنه قال : الحج عرفة ، والعمرة الطواف . وكذا روى الأعمش ، عن إبراهيم عن علقمة في قوله : ( وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله ) قال : هي [ في ] قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت " لا تجاوز بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير ، فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: "'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House, so that one does not exceed the area of the House during the 'Umrah'." Ibrahim then said, "I mentioned this statement to Sa'id bin Jubayr and he said, 'Ibn 'Abbas also said that.'"
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: قراءة عبد الله : " وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) recited it this way: 'Establish [wa-aqimu] Hajj and 'Umrah to the House

variants.variant_arabic: وَأَقِيمُوا الْحَجَّ وَالْعُمْرَةَ إِلَى الْبَيْتِۚ فَإِنۡ أُحۡصِرۡتُمۡ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۖ وَلَا تَحۡلِقُواْ رُءُوسَكُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡلُغَ ٱلۡهَدۡيُ مَحِلَّهُۥۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ بِهِۦٓ أَذٗى مِّن رَّأۡسِهِۦ فَفِدۡيَةٞ مِّن صِيَامٍ أَوۡ صَدَقَةٍ أَوۡ نُسُكٖۚ فَإِذَآ أَمِنتُمۡ فَمَن تَمَتَّعَ بِٱلۡعُمۡرَةِ إِلَى ٱلۡحَجِّ فَمَا ٱسۡتَيۡسَرَ مِنَ ٱلۡهَدۡيِۚ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖ فِي ٱلۡحَجِّ وَسَبۡعَةٍ إِذَا رَجَعۡتُمۡۗ تِلۡكَ عَشَرَةٞ كَامِلَةٞۗ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن لَّمۡ يَكُنۡ أَهۡلُهُۥ حَاضِرِي ٱلۡمَسۡجِدِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ شَدِيدُ ٱلۡعِقَابِ
variants.variant_english: Establish the pilgrimage and the visitation to the House. But if you are prevented, (make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Do not shave your heads until the offering has reached its lawful place. Whoever of you is sick or has an injury to his head, (there is) a ransom of fasting or a freewill offering or a sacrifice. When you are secure, whoever makes use of (the time from) the visitation until the pilgrimage, (let him make) whatever offering is easy to obtain. Whoever cannot find (an offering), (let him perform) a fast of three days during the pilgrimage, and seven (days) when you return. That is ten (days) in all. That is for the one whose family is not present at the Sacred Mosque. Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that God is harsh in retribution.
variants.hadith_arabic: 2599 - حدثني عبيد بن إسماعيل الهباري , قال : ثنا عبد الله بن نمير , عن الأعمش , عن إبراهيم , عن علقمة : { وأتموا الحج والعمرة لله } قال : هو في قراءة عبد الله : { وأقيموا الحج والعمرة إلى البيت } قال : لا تجاوزوا بالعمرة البيت . قال إبراهيم : فذكرت ذلك لسعيد بن جبير , فقال : كذلك قال ابن عباس .

He said: Do not pass beyond the House during the 'Umrah. Ibrahim said: I mentioned that to Sa'id bin Jubayr, and he said: Ibn 'Abbas also said thus.

uthmanic_arabic: لَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحٌ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ فَضۡلٗا مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡۚ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
uthmanic_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Adds 'During the Pilgrimage Seasons' (2:198)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran says 'There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord.' Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr recited an extra phrase at the end: 'during the seasons of the Hajj pilgrimage.'
variants.title: Addition of 'Fi Mawasimi l-Hajj' in Q. 2:198 (Ibn Abbas & Ibn al-Zubayr)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (1770, 2050, 2098, 4519), Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Abbas (as well as 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr and 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud) recited Q. 2:198 with the added prepositional phrase 'فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ' ('during the seasons of the pilgrimage'): 'لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ'. Ibn 'Abbas stated that the verse was revealed with these exact words when early Muslims hesitated to conduct trade at the seasonal markets of 'Ukaz, Majannah, and Dhu al-Majaz during the Hajj.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars classify 'fi mawasimi l-hajj' as an explanatory gloss (qira'ah tafsiriyyah) specifying the time when seeking commercial bounty was questioned, or a phrase whose recitation was abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 2050 and 4519, Ibn 'Abbas explicitly states 'thus the verse was revealed' (fa-nazalat: 'fi mawasimi l-hajj') and continued reciting it that way after the Uthmanic standardization, as did Caliph 'Abdullah bin al-Zubayr in Mecca.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمِجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ تَأَثَّمُوا فِيهِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were marketplaces in the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. When Islam came, Muslims felt that marketing there might be a sin. So, the Divine Inspiration came: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ تَأَثَّمُوا مِنَ التِّجَارَةِ فِيهَا، فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets in the Pre-Islamic period. When the people embraced Islam they considered it a sin to trade there. So, the following Holy Verse came:-- 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَأَنْزَلَ اللَّهُ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ كَذَا
hadiths.highlight_english: 'There is no harm for you if you seek of the bounty of your Lord (Allah) in the Hajj season." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited it like this

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amr bin Dinar from Ibn Abbas
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي مُحَمَّدٌ، قَالَ أَخْبَرَنِي ابْنُ عُيَيْنَةَ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمَجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ فَتَأَثَّمُوا أَنْ يَتَّجِرُوا فِي الْمَوَاسِمِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Mijanna and Dhul-Majaz were markets during the Pre-islamic Period. They (i.e. Muslims) considered it a sin to trade there during the Hajj time (i.e. season), so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ
hadiths.highlight_english: so this Verse was revealed:-- "There is no harm for you if you seek of the Bounty of your Lord during the Hajj season

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt:
3768 - حدثت عن أبي هشام الرفاعي، قال: حدثنا وكيع، عن طلحة بن عمرو، عن عطاء، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
3778 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى، قال: أخبرنا عبد الرزاق، قال: أخبرنا ابن عيينة، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد، قال: سمعت ابن الزبير يقرأ: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
3768 - It was narrated from Abu Hisham al-Rifa'i, from Waki', from Talhah bin 'Amr, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
3778 - Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us... from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid, who said: I heard Ibn al-Zubayr recite: "There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of Hajj.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال وكيع : حدثنا طلحة بن عمرو الحضرمي ، عن عطاء ، عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " . [ وقال عبد الرزاق : عن أبيه عيينة ، عن عبيد الله بن أبي يزيد : سمعت ابن الزبير يقول : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج " ] .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Waki' reported that Talhah bin 'Amr Al-Hadrami narrated from 'Ata' that Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj." 'Abdur-Razzaq reported from his father, from 'Uyaynah, from 'Ubaydullah bin Abi Yazid: I heard Ibn Az-Zubayr say: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ : " ليس عليكم جناح أن تبتغوا فضلا من ربكم في مواسم الحج "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn 'Abbas used to recite: "There is no sin on you in seeking the bounty of your Lord during the seasons of Hajj."

variants.variant_arabic: لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ فَإِذَآ أَفَضۡتُم مِّنۡ عَرَفَٰتٖ فَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ عِندَ ٱلۡمَشۡعَرِ ٱلۡحَرَامِۖ وَٱذۡكُرُوهُ كَمَا هَدَىٰكُمۡ وَإِن كُنتُم مِّن قَبۡلِهِۦ لَمِنَ ٱلضَّآلِّينَ
variants.variant_english: There is no blame on you in seeking favor from your Lord during the seasons of the pilgrimage. When you press on from ‘Arafāt, remember God at the Sacred Monument, and remember Him as He has guided you, though before you were indeed among those who had gone astray.
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنْ عَمْرٍو، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَتْ عُكَاظٌ وَمِجَنَّةُ وَذُو الْمَجَازِ أَسْوَاقًا فِي الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ، فَلَمَّا كَانَ الإِسْلاَمُ فَكَأَنَّهُمْ تَأَثَّمُوا فِيهِ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏لَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ أَنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلاً مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ ‏}‏ فِي مَوَاسِمِ الْحَجِّ، قَرَأَهَا ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:`Ukaz, Majanna and Dhul-Majaz were marketplaces in the Pre-Islamic period of ignorance. When Islam came, Muslims felt that marketing there might be a sin. So, the Divine Inspiration came: "There is no harm for you to seek the bounty of your Lord (in the seasons of Hajj)." (2.198) Ibn `Abbas recited the Verse in this way

uthmanic_arabic: ۞وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فِيٓ أَيَّامٖ مَّعۡدُودَٰتٖۚ فَمَن تَعَجَّلَ فِي يَوۡمَيۡنِ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِ وَمَن تَأَخَّرَ فَلَآ إِثۡمَ عَلَيۡهِۖ لِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰۗ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّكُمۡ إِلَيۡهِ تُحۡشَرُونَ
uthmanic_english: Remember God during a (certain) number of days. Whoever hurries (through it) in two days – no sin (rests) on him, and whoever delays – no sin (rests) on him, (at least) for the one who guards (himself). Guard (yourselves) against God, and know that you will be gathered to Him.

variants.short_title: 'For the One Who Fears God' in 2:203 (Ibn Masud)
variants.plain_english_hook: In the Hajj rites of 2:203, the standard Quran ends the clause with 'for the one who guards (himself)' (liman ittaqa); Ibn Masud's codex added the object 'God' (liman ittaqa Allaha).
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:203 — Addition of 'Allah' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:203, pilgrims departing Mina in two days or delaying have no sin on them 'for the one who guards (himself)' (لِمَنِ اتَّقَىٰ), followed by 'Guard (yourselves) against God' (وَاتَّقُوا اللَّهَ). Al-Tabari records via Ibn Jurayj that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud the first clause explicitly included the divine name: لِمَنِ اتَّقَى اللَّهَ ('for the one who guards (himself) against God').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators regard the addition of 'Allah' after 'liman ittaqa' as making explicit the implied object of piety (taqwa) that immediately follows in 'wattaqu Allaha'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records Ibn Jurayj's direct statement that the word 'Allah' stood in the text of Abdullah bin Mas'ud's Mushaf at this position.

uthmanic_arabic: كَانَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةٗ وَٰحِدَةٗ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ مُبَشِّرِينَ وَمُنذِرِينَ وَأَنزَلَ مَعَهُمُ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ لِيَحۡكُمَ بَيۡنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فِيمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِۚ وَمَا ٱخۡتَلَفَ فِيهِ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُوهُ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مَا جَآءَتۡهُمُ ٱلۡبَيِّنَٰتُ بَغۡيَۢا بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ فَهَدَى ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لِمَا ٱخۡتَلَفُواْ فِيهِ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ بِإِذۡنِهِۦۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُ إِلَىٰ صِرَٰطٖ مُّسۡتَقِيمٍ
uthmanic_english: The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners, and with them He sent down the Book with the truth to judge among the people concerning their differences. Only those who had been given it differed concerning it, after the clear signs had come to them, (because of) envy among themselves. And God guided those who believed to the truth concerning which they differed, by His permission. God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path.

variants.short_title: 'One Community, Then They Differed' in 2:213
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 2:213 jumps directly from 'The people were one community' to 'Then God raised up the prophets'; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices supplied the missing link: 'then they differed'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Baqarah 2:213 — Addition of 'Fa-Ikhtalafu' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 2:213, the verse begins 'The people were (once) one community. Then God raised up the prophets as bringers of good news and warners' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), leaving unstated why prophets were sent if humanity was united. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via authentic chains from Ibn Abbas and Abu al-'Aliyah that the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b explicitly included 'then they differed' (كَانَ النَّاسُ أُمَّةً وَاحِدَةً فَاخْتَلَفُوا فَبَعَثَ اللَّهُ النَّبِيِّينَ), and also note that Ubayy read 'and so that they may be witnesses over the people on the Day of Resurrection' near the end of the verse.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars explain that the Uthmanic text relies on rhetorical ellipsis (idmar) where 'then they differed' is understood from the later phrase 'to judge among the people concerning their differences', while treating the Companion wording as an explanatory gloss.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the authenticated report of Ibn Abbas (graded sahih by al-Hakim) appealing directly to the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('fa-ikhtalafu') to supply the verb required by the narrative logic of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 4048 - حدثنا محمد بن بشار، قال: حدثنا أبو داود، قال: حدثنا همام بن منبه، عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس، قال: كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون، كلهم على شريعة من الحق، فاختلفوا، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين، قال: وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا ". وهي في قراءة أبي بن كعب: ( وليكونوا شهداء على الناس ) يوم القيامة ( والله يهدي من يشاء إلى صراط مستقيم ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 4048 - Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us... from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners. He said: And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed." And it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: {(And so that they would be witnesses over the people)} on the Day of Resurrection {(And God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path)}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: عن عكرمة ، عن ابن عباس ، قال : كان بين نوح وآدم عشرة قرون ، كلهم على شريعة من الحق . فاختلفوا ، فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا " . ورواه الحاكم في مستدركه ، من حديث بندار عن محمد بن بشار . ثم قال : صحيح ولم يخرجاه . وكذا روى أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب : أنه كان يقرؤها : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا فبعث الله النبيين مبشرين ومنذرين " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth. Then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners." He said: "And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'" Al-Hakim recorded it in his Mustadrak... and said: "It is Sahih, though they (Al-Bukhari and Muslim) did not record it." Similarly, Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi narrated from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b, that he used to recite it: "The people were one community, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله : " كان الناس أمة واحدة فاختلفوا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'The people were one community, then they differed.'

variants.hadith_english: 4048 - Muhammad bin Bashshar narrated to us... from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Between Nuh and Adam were ten generations, all of them upon a law of truth, then they differed, so Allah sent the prophets as bringers of good news and warners. He said: And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The people were one community, then they differed." And it is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: {(And so that they would be witnesses over the people)} on the Day of Resurrection {(And God guides whomever He pleases to a straight path)}.

uthmanic_arabic: ٱلطَّلَٰقُ مَرَّتَانِۖ فَإِمۡسَاكُۢ بِمَعۡرُوفٍ أَوۡ تَسۡرِيحُۢ بِإِحۡسَٰنٖۗ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِمَّآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡهِمَا فِيمَا ٱفۡتَدَتۡ بِهِۦۗ تِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِ فَلَا تَعۡتَدُوهَاۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَأُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلظَّـٰلِمُونَ
uthmanic_english: Divorce (may take place) twice, (with the option of) retaining (them) rightfully, or sending (them) away with kindness. It is not permitted to you to take (back) anything of what you have given them, unless the two of them fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God. But if you fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God, (there is) no blame on either of them in what she ransoms (herself) with. Those are the limits (set by) God, so do not transgress them. Whoever transgresses the limits (set by) God, those – they are the evildoers.

variants.short_title: 2:229 — 'Unless They Think' vs. 'Unless They Fear'
variants.plain_english_hook: In the divorce law of 2:229, an ancient Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b replaced 'unless the two of them fear... But if you fear' with 'unless the two of them think... But if the two of them think.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Think' (Yaẓunnā / Ẓannā) for 'Fear' in Ubayy's Mushaf on 2:229
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 2:229, the Uthmanic text governs khul' divorce with the clauses 'إِلَّآ أَن يَخَافَآ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِۖ فَإِنۡ خِفۡتُمۡ أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ' ('unless the two of them fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God. But if you fear that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God'). Al-Tabari (3797) records that Maymun bin Mihran and Ayyub inspected an ancient Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b and found it written: 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَظُنَّا أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ فَإِنْ ظَنَّا أَلَّا يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ اللَّهِ' ('unless the two of them think... But if the two of them think'), while Ibn Mas'ud read 'إِلَّا أَنْ تَخَافُوا' ('unless you [plural] fear').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that classical Arabic poetry occasionally uses 'fear' (khawf) and 'presumption/thought' (ẓann) interchangeably when referring to anticipated future outcomes.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari 3797, Maymun bin Mihran and Ayyub al-Sakhtiyani report physically examining an ancient, reliably transmitted Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b that both replaced the verb root (kh-w-f to ẓ-n-n) and kept the second verb in the dual ('if the two of them think') rather than switching to the second-person plural ('if you fear').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذكر أن ذلك في قراءة أبي بن كعب : " إلا أن يظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله " . 3797 - حدثنا الحسن بن يحيى , قال : أخبرنا عبد الرزاق , قال : أخبرنا معمر , قال : أخبرني ثور , عن ميمون بن مهران , قال : في حرف أبي بن كعب إن الفداء تطليقة . قال : فذكرت ذلك لأيوب , فأتينا رجلا عنده مصحف قديم لأبي خرج من ثقة , فقرأناه فإذا فيه : " إلا أن يظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله , فإن ظنا ألا يقيما حدود الله فلا جناح عليهما فيما افتدت به " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It has been mentioned that this is in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "unless they both presume that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God". 3797 — Al-Hasan bin Yahya narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-Razzaq informed us, he said: Ma'mar informed us, he said: Thawr informed me, from Maymun bin Mihran, who said: In the mode of Ubayy bin Ka'b, the ransom is one pronouncement of divorce. He said: I mentioned that to Ayyub, so we came to a man who had an old Mushaf belonging to Ubayy which emerged from a trustworthy person, and we read it, and in it was: "unless they both presume that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God. But if they presume that they cannot maintain the limits (set by) God, there is no blame on either of them in what she ransoms herself with".

uthmanic_arabic: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
uthmanic_english: Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer. And stand before God obedient.

variants.short_title: Aisha's Codex Adds 'And the Afternoon Prayer' (2:238)
variants.plain_english_hook: While the standard Quran commands believers to guard 'the middle prayer,' Aisha dictated her written Quran codex with the added phrase 'and the afternoon prayer,' stating she heard it from Muhammad.
variants.title: Addition of 'Wa-Salati l-Asr' in the Personal Codex of Aisha (Q. 2:238)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih Muslim 629a, Aisha's freedman Abu Yunus reports that Aisha ordered him to transcribe a personal Mushaf for her and explicitly instructed him to write Q. 2:238 with the additional conjunction and phrase 'وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ' ('and the afternoon prayer'), affirming that she heard it directly from the Prophet. Because the conjunctive particle 'wa-' ('and') grammatically distinguishes the Afternoon ('Asr) prayer from the 'middle prayer' (al-salat al-wusta), this reading directly impacted early legal debates over which of the five daily prayers is the middle prayer.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and the middle prayer.
variants.variant_target_english: and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer.
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ ٱلۡوُسۡطَىٰ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer. And stand before God obedient.
variants.variant_full_arabic: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
variants.variant_full_english: Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer. And stand before God obedient.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators argue that the additional wording was either an explanatory gloss (qira'ah tafsiriyyah) identifying the middle prayer or an earlier recitation whose wording was later abrogated (naskh al-tilawah) as reported via al-Bara' bin 'Azib in Sahih Muslim 630.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih Muslim 629a, Aisha dictates this wording into her physical Mushaf after the Prophet's death—when abrogation could no longer occur—and both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir note that the conjunctive 'wa-' ('and the afternoon prayer') grammatically implies a second prayer rather than a simple equating gloss.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى التَّمِيمِيُّ، قَالَ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى مَالِكٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنِ الْقَعْقَاعِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي يُونُسَ، مَوْلَى عَائِشَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ أَمَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ لَهَا مُصْحَفًا وَقَالَتْ إِذَا بَلَغْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ فَآذِنِّي ‏{‏ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى‏}‏ فَلَمَّا بَلَغْتُهَا آذَنْتُهَا فَأَمْلَتْ عَلَىَّ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ ‏.‏ وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Abu Yunus, the freed slave of 'A'isha said:'A'isha ordered me to transcribe a copy of the Qur'an for her and said: When you reach this verse:" Guard the prayers and the middle prayer" (ii. 238), inform me; so when I reached it, I informed her and she gave me dictation (like this): Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer, and stand up truly obedient to Allah. 'A'isha said: This is how I have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَأَمْلَتْ عَلَىَّ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ ‏.‏ وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ
hadiths.highlight_english: Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer, and stand up truly obedient to Allah.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt:
4216 - حدثنا ابن المثنى، قال: ثنا عبد الوهاب، قال: ثنا أيوب، عن أبي قلابة، عن أبي يونس مولى عائشة، أنه قال: أمرتني عائشة أن أكتب لها مصحفًا، وقالت: إذا بلغت هذه الآية فآذنِّي: " حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى "، فلما بلغتها آذنتها، فأملت عليَّ: " حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وصلاة العصر وقوموا لله قانتين "، وقالت: سمعتها من رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم.
4220 - حدثني المثنى، قال: ثنا الحجاج، قال: ثنا حماد، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه، قال: كان في مصحف عائشة: " حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وهي صلاة العصر ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
4216 - Ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us... from Abu Yunus, the freed slave of 'A'ishah, that he said: 'A'ishah ordered me to write a Mushaf for her, and she said: When you reach this verse, let me know: "Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer." When I reached it, I let her know, and she dictated to me: "Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the 'Asr prayer, and stand before God obedient," and she said: I heard it from the Messenger of God, peace and blessings of God be upon him.
4220 - Al-Muthanna narrated to me... from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: It was in the Mushaf of 'A'ishah: "Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and it is the 'Asr prayer."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فأملت عليَّ: " حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وصلاة العصر وقوموا لله قانتين "

tafsir_sources.scholar_name: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (d. 774 AH) — Aisha's Mushaf
tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال ابن جرير : حدثني المثنى ، حدثنا الحجاج ، حدثنا حماد ، عن هشام بن عروة عن أبيه قال : كان في مصحف عائشة : " حافظوا على الصلوات والصلاة الوسطى وهي صلاة العصر " ... وأما إن روي على أنه قرآن فإنه لم يتواتر ، فلا يثبت بمثل خبر الواحد قرآن ; ولهذا لم يثبته أمير المؤمنين عثمان بن عفان في المصحف الإمام .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jarir said: Al-Muthanna narrated to me, Al-Hajjaj narrated to us, Hammad narrated to us, from Hisham bin 'Urwah from his father who said: "It was in the Mushaf of 'A'ishah: 'Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and it is the 'Asr prayer.'" ... As for if it is narrated as being from the Quran, it is not Mutawatir (widely transmitted), and the Quran is not established by an isolated report (Khabar Al-Wahid). This is why the Commander of the Faithful 'Uthman bin 'Affan did not include it in the 'Imam' (master) Mushaf.

tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It was in the Mushaf of 'A'ishah: 'Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and it is the 'Asr prayer.'

variants.variant_arabic: حَٰفِظُواْ عَلَى ٱلصَّلَوَٰتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ وَقُومُواْ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ
variants.variant_english: Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer. And stand before God obedient.
variants.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى التَّمِيمِيُّ، قَالَ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى مَالِكٍ عَنْ زَيْدِ بْنِ أَسْلَمَ، عَنِ الْقَعْقَاعِ بْنِ حَكِيمٍ، عَنْ أَبِي يُونُسَ، مَوْلَى عَائِشَةَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ أَمَرَتْنِي عَائِشَةُ أَنْ أَكْتُبَ لَهَا مُصْحَفًا وَقَالَتْ إِذَا بَلَغْتَ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ فَآذِنِّي ‏{‏ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى‏}‏ فَلَمَّا بَلَغْتُهَا آذَنْتُهَا فَأَمْلَتْ عَلَىَّ حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ ‏.‏ وَقُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَانِتِينَ ‏.‏ قَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Abu Yunus, the freed slave of 'A'isha said:'A'isha ordered me to transcribe a copy of the Qur'an for her and said: When you reach this verse:" Guard the prayers and the middle prayer" (ii. 238), inform me; so when I reached it, I informed her and she gave me dictation (like this): Guard the prayers and the middle prayer and the afternoon prayer, and stand up truly obedient to Allah. 'A'isha said: This is how I have heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)

variants.short_title: Hafsa's Codex Adds 'And the Afternoon Prayer' (2:238)
variants.plain_english_hook: Hafsa, custodian of the first Quranic sheets, ordered her scribe to write verse 2:238 in her personal codex with the extra phrase 'and the afternoon prayer,' which Nafi' personally saw in her Mushaf.
variants.title: Addition of 'Wa-Salati l-Asr' in the Personal Codex of Hafsa bint Umar (Q. 2:238)
variants.diff_summary: Multiple authentic chains in Tafsir al-Tabari and Muwatta Malik (via 'Amr bin Rafi', Salim bin 'Abdullah, and Nafi' the freedman of Ibn 'Umar) record that Hafsa bint 'Umar—the wife of the Prophet and custodian of Abu Bakr's original Quranic sheets—instructed her scribe to pause at Q. 2:238 so she could dictate it as she heard the Prophet recite it: 'حَافِظُوا عَلَى الصَّلَوَاتِ وَالصَّلاَةِ الْوُسْطَى وَصَلاَةِ الْعَصْرِ' ('Watch over the prayers, and the middle prayer, and the afternoon prayer'). Nafi' explicitly testified: 'I read that Mushaf and I saw the conjunctive waw in it.'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators such as Ibn Kathir argue that Hafsa's dictation represented either an abrogated recitation (mansukh al-tilawah) or an interpretive note recorded via single-strand transmission (khabar al-wahid) and therefore omitted by Uthman from the master Mushaf.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Hafsa was the very custodian from whom Caliph Uthman borrowed the first written collection (suhuf) to produce the Uthmanic standard, yet she deliberately dictated this additional phrase into her own Mushaf as verbatim prophetic recitation, and Nafi' verified seeing the consonantal letter waw written in her codex.

uthmanic_arabic: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةٞ وَلَا نَوۡمٞۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءٖ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
uthmanic_english: God – (there is) no god but Him, the Living, the Everlasting. Slumber does not overtake Him, nor sleep. To Him (belongs) whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. variants.short_title: Umar's Reading 'Al-Qayyam' in the Verse of the Throne
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 7442 and Tafsir al-Tabari, Caliph Umar bin Al-Khattab and Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited the Verse of the Throne (2:255) with 'al-Qayyām' (with an alif) instead of 'al-Qayyūm' (with a waw).
variants.title: Recitation of 'Al-Hayyu al-Qayyam' Instead of 'Al-Hayyu al-Qayyum' in Surah 2:255
variants.diff_summary: In the famous Verse of the Throne (Ayat al-Kursi, 2:255, and its parallel in 3:2), the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'al-Ḥayyu al-Qayyūm' ('the Living, the Everlasting') on the morphological pattern fay'ūl (written with a wāw). However, Imam al-Bukhari records in Sahih al-Bukhari 7442 that Caliph Umar bin Al-Khattab recited 'al-Qayyām' (on the pattern fay'āl, written with an alif), and al-Tabari (under 3:2) documents that both Umar bin Al-Khattab and Abdullah bin Mas'ud read 'al-Ḥayyu al-Qayyām' (while Ibn Mas'ud's disciple Alqamah also read 'al-Qayyim').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Imam al-Bukhari remarks that 'both are expressions of praise' (wa-kilāhumā madḥ), and al-Tabari explains that 'al-Qayyām' reflects the Hijazi dialectal preference for the fay'āl pattern in hollow roots while affirming that only the Uthmanic 'al-Qayyūm' is permissible to recite today.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit ruling under 3:2—that no reading other than 'al-Qayyūm' is permissible because it is what was established in the Uthmanic codices—acknowledges that the non-Uthmanic consonantal spelling 'al-Qayyām' recited by Caliph Umar and Ibn Mas'ud was excluded by the Uthmanic rasm.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي ثَابِتُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، عَنْ سُلَيْمَانَ الأَحْوَلِ، عَنْ طَاوُسٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم إِذَا تَهَجَّدَ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ قَالَ ‏ "‏ اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّنَا لَكَ الْحَمْدُ، أَنْتَ قَيِّمُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، وَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ أَنْتَ نُورُ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالأَرْضِ وَمَنْ فِيهِنَّ، أَنْتَ الْحَقُّ، وَقَوْلُكَ الْحَقُّ، وَوَعْدُكَ الْحَقُّ، وَلِقَاؤُكَ الْحَقُّ، وَالْجَنَّةُ حَقٌّ، وَالنَّارُ حَقٌّ، وَالسَّاعَةُ حَقٌّ، اللَّهُمَّ لَكَ أَسْلَمْتُ، وَبِكَ آمَنْتُ، وَعَلَيْكَ تَوَكَّلْتُ، وَإِلَيْكَ خَاصَمْتُ، وَبِكَ حَاكَمْتُ، فَاغْفِرْ لِي مَا قَدَّمْتُ وَمَا أَخَّرْتُ، وَأَسْرَرْتُ وَأَعْلَنْتُ، وَمَا أَنْتَ أَعْلَمُ بِهِ مِنِّي، لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ أَنْتَ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ قَيْسُ بْنُ سَعْدٍ وَأَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ عَنْ طَاوُسٍ قَيَّامٌ‏.‏ وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ الْقَيُّومُ الْقَائِمُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَىْءٍ‏.‏ وَقَرَأَ عُمَرُ الْقَيَّامُ، وَكِلاَهُمَا مَدْحٌ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:Whenever the Prophet (ﷺ) offered his Tahajjud prayer, he would say, "O Allah, our Lord! All the praises are for You; You are the Keeper (Establisher or the One Who looks after) of the Heavens and the Earth. All the Praises are for You; You are the Light of the Heavens and the Earth and whatever is therein. You are the Truth, and Your saying is the Truth, and Your promise is the Truth, and the meeting with You is the Truth, and Paradise is the Truth, and the (Hell) Fire is the Truth. O Allah! I surrender myself to You, and believe in You, and I put my trust in You (solely depend upon). And to You I complain of my opponents and with Your Evidence I argue. So please forgive the sins which I have done in the past or I will do in the future, and also those (sins) which I did in secret or in public, and that which You know better than I. None has the right to be worshipped but You [Al-Bukhari added: And Umar recited Al-Qayyam, and both are praise.]
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَقَرَأَ عُمَرُ الْقَيَّامُ، وَكِلاَهُمَا مَدْحٌ
hadiths.highlight_english: And Umar recited Al-Qayyam, and both are praise.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: فقوله : ( الله لا إله إلا هو ) إخبار بأنه المتفرد بالإلهية لجميع الخلائق ( الحي القيوم ) أي : الحي في نفسه الذي لا يموت أبدا القيم لغيره ، وكان عمر يقرأ : " القيام " فجميع الموجودات مفتقرة إليه وهو غني عنها ، ولا قوام لها بدون أمره .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: His statement: {Allah! None has the right to be worshipped but He} informs that He alone is the Deity of all creation. {The Ever-Living, the Sustainer (Al-Qayyum)} testifies that He is the Ever-Living in Himself, Who never dies, the Sustainer of others. 'Umar used to recite it as: "Al-Qayyam". All existing things stand in need of Him, and He is free of need from them, and they have no existence without His command.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وكان عمر يقرأ : " القيام "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Umar used to recite it as: "Al-Qayyam".

uthmanic_arabic: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتٞ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتٞۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغٞ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلّٞ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
uthmanic_english: He (it is) who has sent down on you the Book, of which some verses are clearly composed – they are the mother of the Book – but others are ambiguous. As for those in whose hearts (there is) a turning aside, they follow the ambiguous part of it, seeking (to cause) trouble and seeking its interpretation. No one knows its interpretation except God. And (as for) the ones firmly grounded in knowledge, they say, ‘We believe in it. All (of it) is from our Lord.’ Yet no one takes heed except those with understanding.

variants.short_title: Who Knows the Ambiguous Verses in 3:7?
variants.plain_english_hook: Scholars debated for centuries where the sentence breaks in 3:7; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices worded the clause so that only God knows the ambiguous verses' interpretation.
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:7 — Syntactic Separation of 'Those Firm in Knowledge'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:7 (وَمَا يَعْلَمُ تَأْوِيلَهُ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), exegetes and theologians were divided over whether 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge' is conjoined to 'God' (meaning scholars also know the interpretation of ambiguous verses) or begins a new sentence. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud's reading was 'Its interpretation is only with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say, We believe in it' (إِنْ تَأْوِيلُهُ إِلَّا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ وَالرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ يَقُولُونَ آمَنَّا بِهِ), while Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'and those firmly grounded in knowledge say' (وَيَقُولُ الرَّاسِخُونَ فِي الْعِلْمِ), both syntactically precluding conjunction with God.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: No one knows its interpretation except God.
variants.variant_target_english: Its interpretation is only with God.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators cite the readings of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b as explanatory recitations (qira'at tafsiriyya) proving that a mandatory pause (waqf) falls after the name of God in the Uthmanic text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explicitly rely on the non-Uthmanic wording of Ibn Mas'ud ('in ta'wiluhu illa 'inda Allah') and Ubayy bin Ka'b ('wa yaqulu al-rasikhuna') to settle a foundational theological dispute over whether human scholars can know the ta'wil of the mutashabihat.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وهو فيما بلغني مع ذلك في قراءة أبي : " ويقول الراسخون في العلم " كما ذكرناه عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤه ; وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And that is, along with that, according to what reached me regarding the recitation of Ubayy: "and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say", just as we mentioned it from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it; and in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say".
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وفي قراءة عبد الله : إن تأويله إلا عند الله " والراسخون في العلم يقولون "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: "its interpretation is not except with God, and the ones firmly grounded in knowledge say"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وحكى ابن جرير أن في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إن تأويله إلا عند الله والراسخون في العلم يقولون آمنا به " . وكذا عن أبي بن كعب . واختار ابن جرير هذا القول .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jarir narrated that in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is: "Its interpretation is only with Allah, and those who are firmly grounded in knowledge say: 'We believe in it.'" And similarly it was narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b. Ibn Jarir preferred this opinion.

uthmanic_arabic: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَكۡفُرُونَ بِـَٔايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَيَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلَّذِينَ يَأۡمُرُونَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ مِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ فَبَشِّرۡهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ
uthmanic_english: Surely those who disbelieve in the signs of God, and kill the prophets without any right, and kill those of the people who command justice – give them news of a painful punishment.

variants.short_title: 'And Fought' (Wa-Qatalu) vs 'And Kill' in 3:21
variants.plain_english_hook: In 3:21, the standard Quran says 'and kill those of the people who command justice'; al-Tabari records that in Ibn Masud's codex it was written 'and fought' (wa-qatalu).
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:21 — 'Wa-Qatalu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs 'Wa-Yaqtuluna'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:21, those who disbelieve are condemned because they kill the prophets and 'kill those of the people who command justice' (وَيَقْتُلُونَ الَّذِينَ يَأْمُرُونَ بِالْقِسْطِ مِنَ النَّاسِ). Al-Tabari records that some Kufan reciters read 'and fight' (وَيُقَاتِلُونَ) based on the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, in which the verb was written in the past tense Form III: وَقَاتَلُوا ('and fought').

variants.variant_target_english: and fought those of the people who command justice

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari rejects the Kufan reading 'wa-yuqatiluna' and the appeal to Ibn Mas'ud's codex, maintaining that the consensus of the authoritative reciters across the garrison cities establishes 'wa-yaqtuluna' (and kill).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's testimony again illustrates how Kufan reciters attempted to bridge the gap between Ibn Mas'ud's codex ('wa-qatalu', Form III past tense) and the Uthmanic rasm by reading Form III imperfect ('wa-yuqatiluna').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأه بعض المتأخرين من قرأة الكوفة: ( ويقاتلون )، بمعنى القتال، تأولا منه قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود، وادعى أن ذلك في مصحف عبد الله: ( وقاتلوا )، فقرأ الذي وصفنا أمره من القراءة بذلك التأويل: ( ويقاتلون ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the later reciters of Kufa recited it: (*wa yuqātilūna* - *and they fight*), in the meaning of fighting, interpreting from it the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud, and he claimed that this was [written] in the codex of 'Abdullah: (*wa qātalū* - *and they fought*), so the one whose matter of recitation we described read with that interpretation: (*wa yuqātilūna*).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف عبد الله: ( وقاتلوا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the codex of 'Abdullah: (*wa qātalū* - *and they fought*)

uthmanic_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
uthmanic_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’

variants.short_title: 3:81 — Covenant of the Book's People vs. Prophets
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says God took a covenant with 'the prophets,' Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'those who were given the Book,' with Mujahid calling 'prophets' a scribal error.
variants.title: Substitution of 'Those Given the Book' for 'The Prophets' in 3:81
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 3:81, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَٰقَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ' ('when God took a covenant with the prophets'). Al-Tabari records via two authentic chains from Mujahid (7323–7324) and from al-Rabi' bin Anas (7325) that in the recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b it read 'وَإِذْ أَخَذَ اللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ' ('when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book').

variants.variant_target_english: a covenant with those who were given the Book
