scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari argues that single-chain reports attributing variant readings or scribal errors to Companions cannot override the consensus codex, and later editors suggest Mujahid only meant the scribe wrote an earlier recitation instead of the final review.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari 7323–7324, Mujahid explicitly states regarding 'covenant with the prophets': 'It is an error from the scribe (هي خطأ من الكاتب), and in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud it is: And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7323 - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة "، قال: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ". (37) 7325 - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع في قوله: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين "، يقول: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب، وكذلك كان يقرؤها الربيع: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "، إنما هي أهل الكتاب. قال: وكذلك كان يقرأها أبي بن كعب.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **7323** - *Muhammad bin ‘Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying:* "(Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom’", he said: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." 7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets", he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book," and thus Al-Rabi' used to recite it. He said: And thus Ubayy bin Ka'b used to recite it as well.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book."

variants.variant_arabic: وَإِذۡ أَخَذَ ٱللَّهُ مِيثَاقَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ لَمَآ ءَاتَيۡتُكُم مِّن كِتَٰبٖ وَحِكۡمَةٖ ثُمَّ جَآءَكُمۡ رَسُولٞ مُّصَدِّقٞ لِّمَا مَعَكُمۡ لَتُؤۡمِنُنَّ بِهِۦ وَلَتَنصُرُنَّهُۥۚ قَالَ ءَأَقۡرَرۡتُمۡ وَأَخَذۡتُمۡ عَلَىٰ ذَٰلِكُمۡ إِصۡرِيۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَقۡرَرۡنَاۚ قَالَ فَٱشۡهَدُواْ وَأَنَا۠ مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلشَّـٰهِدِينَ
variants.variant_english: (Remember) when God took a covenant with those who were given the Book: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom, when a messenger comes to you confirming what is with you, you are to believe in him and you are to help him.’ He said, ‘Do you agree and accept My burden on that (condition)?’ They said, ‘We agree.’ He said, ‘Bear witness, and I shall be with you among the witnesses.’
variants.hadith_arabic: 7323 - حدثني محمد بن عمرو قال، حدثنا أبو عاصم، عن عيسى، عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد في قوله: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق النبيين لما آتيتكم من كتاب وحكمة "، قال: هي خطأ من الكاتب، وهي في قراءة ابن مسعود: " وإذ أخذَ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب ". (37) 7325 - حدثني المثنى قال، حدثنا إسحاق قال، حدثنا عبد الله بن أبي جعفر، عن أبيه، عن الربيع في قوله: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق النبيين "، يقول: وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب، وكذلك كان يقرؤها الربيع: " وإذ أخذ الله ميثاق الذين أوتوا الكتاب "، إنما هي أهل الكتاب. قال: وكذلك كان يقرأها أبي بن كعب.
variants.hadith_english: **7323** - *Muhammad bin ‘Amr narrated to me, he said: Abu ‘Asim narrated to us, from ‘Isa, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid regarding His saying:* "(Remember) when God took a covenant with the prophets: ‘Whatever indeed I have given you of the Book and wisdom’", he said: It is an error from the scribe, and it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas‘ud: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book." 7325 — Al-Muthanna narrated to me, saying: Ishaq narrated to us, saying: 'Abdullah bin Abi Ja'far narrated to us, from his father, from Al-Rabi' regarding His saying: "And when God took the covenant of the prophets", he says: "And when God took the covenant of those who were given the Book," and thus Al-Rabi' used to recite it. He said: And thus Ubayy bin Ka'b used to recite it as well.

uthmanic_arabic: لَّقَدۡ سَمِعَ ٱللَّهُ قَوۡلَ ٱلَّذِينَ قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ فَقِيرٞ وَنَحۡنُ أَغۡنِيَآءُۘ سَنَكۡتُبُ مَا قَالُواْ وَقَتۡلَهُمُ ٱلۡأَنۢبِيَآءَ بِغَيۡرِ حَقّٖ وَنَقُولُ ذُوقُواْ عَذَابَ ٱلۡحَرِيقِ
uthmanic_english: Certainly God has heard the words of those who said, ‘Surely God is poor and we are rich.’ We shall write down what they have said, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and We shall say, ‘Taste the punishment of the burning (Fire)!

variants.short_title: 'It Will Be Written' vs 'We Shall Write' in 3:181
variants.plain_english_hook: In 3:181, the standard Quran reads in the first-person plural 'We shall write... and We shall say' (wa-naqulu); Ibn Masud's codex had the passive 'and it will be said' (wa-yuqalu).
variants.title: Surah Al 'Imran 3:181 — Passive 'Sayuktabu... wa-Yuqalu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Codex
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 3:181, the majority of reciters read in the first-person plural active: سَنَكْتُبُ مَا قَالُوا وَقَتْلَهُمُ الْأَنْبِيَاءَ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ وَنَقُولُ ('We shall write down what they have said, along with their killing the prophets without any right, and We shall say'). Al-Tabari notes that the Kufan canonical reciter Hamzah read the passive سَيُكْتَبُ ('will be written') and nominative وَقَتْلُهُمُ by relying on the Mushaf and recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, which read سَيُكْتَبُ ... وَيُقَالُ ('will be written ... and it will be said', with ya' and alif in 'yuqalu' instead of nun and waw in 'naqulu').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Supporters of Hamzah's canonical reading argue that the shift from passive 'sayuktabu' to first-person active 'wa-naqulu' is an instance of rhetorical person-shifting (iltifat) necessitated by the Uthmanic rasm.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari criticizes Hamzah's hybrid reading for adopting the passive beginning ('sayuktabu') from Ibn Mas'ud's codex while being forced by the Uthmanic rasm to abandon Ibn Mas'ud's matching passive continuation ('wa-yuqalu').

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ذلك بعض قرأة الكوفيين: ( " سيكتب ما قالوا وقتلهم الأنبياء بغير حق " ) بالياء من " سيكتب " وبضمها، ورفع " القتل "، على مذهب ما لم يسم فاعله، اعتبارا بقراءة يذكر أنها من قراءة عبد الله في قوله: " ونقول ذوقوا "، يذكر أنها في قراءة عبد الله: " ويقال". فأغفل قارئ ذلك وجه الصواب فيما قصد إليه من تأويل القراءة التي تنسب إلى عبد الله، وخالف الحجة من قرأة الإسلام.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the Kufan reciters recited that: ("What they have said will be written down [sayuktabu], and their killing [wa-qatluhumu] the prophets without right") with a ya' in 'sayuktabu' and a dammah on it, and the nominative in 'al-qatl', in the passive voice, by analogy with a recitation mentioned to be from the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud] in His saying: 'and We shall say, Taste', which is mentioned to be in the recitation of 'Abdullah: 'and it will be said [wa-yuqalu]'. Thus the reciter of that overlooked the correct aspect in what he intended of interpreting the recitation attributed to 'Abdullah.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: " ويقال"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: 'and it will be said [wa-yuqalu]'

uthmanic_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَرِثُواْ ٱلنِّسَآءَ كَرۡهٗاۖ وَلَا تَعۡضُلُوهُنَّ لِتَذۡهَبُواْ بِبَعۡضِ مَآ ءَاتَيۡتُمُوهُنَّ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ وَعَاشِرُوهُنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ فَإِن كَرِهۡتُمُوهُنَّ فَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـٔٗا وَيَجۡعَلَ ٱللَّهُ فِيهِ خَيۡرٗا كَثِيرٗا
uthmanic_english: You who believe! It is not permitted to you to inherit women against their will. And do not prevent them, so that you may take part of what you have given them, unless they commit clear immorality. Associate with them rightfully. If you dislike them, it may be that you dislike something in which God has placed much good.

variants.short_title: 4:19 — 'Unless They Act Insolently' vs. 'Immorality'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran allows taking back a wife's dowry only if 'they commit clear immorality,' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read the single verb 'unless they act insolently.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Unless They Act Insolently' (Illā An Yafḥushna) in 4:19
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 4:19, the Uthmanic text forbids husbands from pressuring wives to forfeit part of their dowries 'إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ' ('unless they commit clear immorality.'). Al-Tabari (3816, 8900) records from Miqsam that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this clause read 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَ' ('unless they act insolently.')—along with 'وَلَا أَنْ تَعْضُلُوهُنَّ' earlier in the verse—which Miqsam cited to show that verbal insolence and disobedience suffice to make a khul' ransom lawful.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Jurists who interpret 'clear immorality' (fāḥisha mubayyina) as encompassing marital defiance and verbal abuse (bhadhā' al-lisān) view Ibn Mas'ud's verb 'yafḥushna' as an explanatory reading supporting that broader legal definition.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'إِلَّا أَنْ يَفْحُشْنَ' twice (under both 2:229 and 4:19), where the three-word Uthmanic noun phrase 'commit clear immorality' is replaced by a single intransitive verb meaning to speak or act insolently.

uthmanic_english: And if you wish to exchange a wife for (another) wife, and you have given one of them a qinṭr, take (back) none of it. Would you take it (back by) slander and clear sin?

variants.short_title: 'A Qintar of Gold' & 'Not Lawful to Take' in 4:20
variants.plain_english_hook: When a woman challenged Umar's cap on marriage dowries using 4:20, she and Ibn Masud's recitation read 'a qintar of gold, it is not lawful for you to take any of it'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:20 — 'Qintaran min Dhahabin' in Ibn Mas'ud's Recitation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:20, husbands wishing to divorce and remarry are told: 'and you have given one of them a qintar, take (back) none of it' (وَآتَيْتُمْ إِحْدَاهُنَّ قِنْطَارًا فَلَا تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا). Ibn Kathir records in the famous report of Umar bin al-Khattab and the woman who objected to his dowry restriction that the verse was recited with 'a qintar of gold' (قِنْطَارًا مِنْ ذَهَبٍ) and that in Abdullah bin Mas'ud's recitation it read: 'it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it' (فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمْ أَنْ تَأْخُذُوا مِنْهُ شَيْئًا).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a qinṭr, take (back) none of it
variants.variant_target_arabic: قِنطَارٗا مِّن ذَهَبٍ فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔا
variants.variant_target_english: a qintar of gold, then it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجٖ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجٖ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارٗا فَلَا تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنٗا وَإِثۡمٗا مُّبِينٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: And if you wish to exchange a wife for (another) wife, and you have given one of them a qinṭr, take (back) none of it. Would you take it (back by) slander and clear sin?
variants.variant_full_arabic: وَإِنۡ أَرَدتُّمُ ٱسۡتِبۡدَالَ زَوۡجٖ مَّكَانَ زَوۡجٖ وَءَاتَيۡتُمۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُنَّ قِنطَارٗا مِّن ذَهَبٍ فَلَا يَحِلُّ لَكُمۡ أَن تَأۡخُذُواْ مِنۡهُ شَيۡـًٔاۚ أَتَأۡخُذُونَهُۥ بُهۡتَٰنٗا وَإِثۡمٗا مُّبِينٗا
variants.variant_full_english: And if you wish to exchange a wife for (another) wife, and you have given one of them a qintar of gold, then it is not lawful for you to take (back) any of it. Would you take it (back by) slander and clear sin?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars treat 'min dhahabin' (of gold) and 'fa-la yahillu lakum an' (it is not lawful for you to) as explanatory glosses clarifying the value of a qintar and the prohibitive force of 'fa-la ta'khudhu'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The narration preserved by Ibn Kathir links both phrase expansions directly to the public legal exchange with Caliph Umar and explicitly attests 'fa-la yahillu lakum an ta'khudhu minhu shay'an' as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال عمر بن الخطاب : لا تغالوا في مهور النساء . فقالت امرأة : ليس ذلك لك يا عمر ، إن الله تعالى يقول : " وآتيتم إحداهن قنطارا من ذهب " . قال : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فلا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا منه شيئا " فقال عمر : إن امرأة خاصمت عمر فخصمته .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said: 'Do not be excessive in the dowries of women.' A woman said: 'You do not have that right, O 'Umar, for Allah the Exalted says: "and you have given one of them a Qintar of gold."' He (the narrator) said: 'And likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "so it is not lawful for you to take any of it."' Thereupon 'Umar said: 'Indeed, a woman disputed with 'Umar and defeated him in argument.'
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فلا يحل لكم أن تأخذوا منه شيئا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "so it is not lawful for you to take any of it."

uthmanic_arabic: ۞وَٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتُ مِنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُكُمۡۖ كِتَٰبَ ٱللَّهِ عَلَيۡكُمۡۚ وَأُحِلَّ لَكُم مَّا وَرَآءَ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَن تَبۡتَغُواْ بِأَمۡوَٰلِكُم مُّحۡصِنِينَ غَيۡرَ مُسَٰفِحِينَۚ فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ فَـَٔاتُوهُنَّ أُجُورَهُنَّ فَرِيضَةٗۚ وَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ فِيمَا تَرَٰضَيۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ٱلۡفَرِيضَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمٗا
uthmanic_english: And (also forbidden to you are) married women, except what your right (hands) own. (This is) a written decree of God for you. (All women) beyond that are permitted to you to seek (to obtain) by means of your wealth, taking (them) in marriage, not in immorality. So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation. (There is) no blame on you in anything you may give them by mutual agreement beyond this obligation. Surely God is knowing, wise.

variants.short_title: 4:24 — 'For a Specified Term' in Marriage
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'what you enjoy from them, give them their marriage gifts,' Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Abbas read 'what you enjoy from them for a specified term.'
variants.title: Addition of 'For a Specified Term' (Ilā Ajalin Musammā) in 4:24
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 4:24, the Uthmanic text reads 'فَمَا ٱسۡتَمۡتَعۡتُم بِهِۦ مِنۡهُنَّ' ('So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b and the recitation of Ibn Abbas added the legal stipulation 'إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى' ('for a specified term'), with Ibn Abbas swearing three times that God revealed the verse with this phrase.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَمَا اسْتَمْتَعْتُمْ بِهِ مِنْهُنَّ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى
variants.variant_target_english: So (because of) what you enjoy from them in this way for a specified term

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Sunni commentators argue that the phrase 'for a specified term' was either an explanatory gloss (qirā'a tafsīriyya) referring to early temporary marriage (mut'ah) or a wording whose recitation and legal ruling were subsequently abrogated.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tafsir al-Tabari (7181–7182), witnesses testify to physically inspecting the written Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b containing the phrase, and when Abu Nadrah objected that he did not read it that way, Ibn Abbas swore by God three times that God revealed it thus.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 7181 - حدثنا أبو كريب , قال : ثنا يحيى بن عيسى , قال : ثنا نصير بن أبي الأشعث , قال : ثني حبيب بن أبي ثابت , عن أبيه , قال : أعطاني ابن عباس مصحفا , فقال : هذا على قراءة أبي . قال أبو كريب , قال يحيى : فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " . 7184 - حدثنا ابن بشار , قال : ثنا عبد الأعلى , قال : ثنا سعيد , عن قتادة , قال : في قراءة أبي بن كعب : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 7181 - Abu Kurayb narrated to us, he said: Yahya bin 'Isa narrated to us, he said: Nusayr bin Abi Al-Ash'ath narrated to us, he said: Habib bin Abi Thabit narrated to me, from his father, he said: Ibn 'Abbas gave me a Mus-haf and said: This is according to the recitation of Ubayy. Abu Kurayb said, Yahya said: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term." 7184 - Ibn Bashshar narrated to us, he said: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, he said: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, he said: In the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فرأيت المصحف عند نصير فيه : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: So I saw the Mus-haf with Nusayr, and in it was: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them to a specified term."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد روي عن ابن عباس وطائفة من الصحابة القول بإباحتها للضرورة ، وهو رواية عن الإمام أحمد بن حنبل ، رحمهم الله تعالى . وكان ابن عباس ، وأبي بن كعب ، وسعيد بن جبير ، والسدي يقرءون : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة " . وقال مجاهد : نزلت في نكاح المتعة ، ولكن الجمهور على خلاف ذلك ، والعمدة ما ثبت في الصحيحين ، عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب [ رضي الله عنه ] قال : نهى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نكاح المتعة وعن لحوم الحمر الأهلية يوم خيبر ولهذا الحديث ألفاظ مقررة هي في كتاب " الأحكام " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and a group of the Companions the view that it was permitted out of necessity, and it is a narration from Imam Ahmad bin Hanbal (may Allah have mercy on them). Ibn 'Abbas, Ubayy bin Ka'b, Sa'id bin Jubayr, and As-Suddi used to recite: "So (because of) what you enjoy from them *until a specified time*, give them their marriage gifts as an obligation." Mujahid stated that it was revealed about the Mut'ah marriage. But the majority are against that.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وكان ابن عباس ، وأبي بن كعب ، وسعيد بن جبير ، والسدي يقرءون : " فما استمتعتم به منهن إلى أجل مسمى فآتوهن أجورهن فريضة "

variants.short_title: Aisha's Codex: 'Idols' Instead of 'Females' (4:117)
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran states that pagans call only upon 'females' (inathan) besides God; in Aisha's personal codex, the word was written 'idols' (awthanan).
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:117 — 'Awthanan' (Idols) in Aisha's Mushaf vs 'Inathan'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:117, polytheists are described as calling only upon 'females' (إِنَاثًا, referring to female-named deities such as al-Lat, al-'Uzza, and Manat) instead of God. Al-Tabari records with a direct chain through Hisham bin 'Urwah from his father 'Urwah bin al-Zubayr that in the Mushaf of Aisha it was written 'They only call on idols instead of Him' (إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلَّا أَوْثَانًا), and notes a related reading from Ibn Abbas ('uthunan', plural of wathan, idol).
variants.uthmanic_target_english: on females
variants.variant_target_english: on idols
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ إِنَٰثٗا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَٰنٗا مَّرِيدٗا
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They only call on females instead of Him. They only call on a rebellious Satan.
variants.variant_full_arabic: إِن يَدۡعُونَ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ إِلَّآ أَوۡثَٰنٗا وَإِن يَدۡعُونَ إِلَّا شَيۡطَٰنٗا مَّرِيدٗا
variants.variant_full_english: They only call on idols instead of Him. They only call on a rebellious Satan.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari maintains that the Uthmanic reading 'inathan' (females) must be followed due to the consensus of the regional Mushafs, explaining that the pagan Arabs gave their idols female names and called the angels daughters of God.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The transmission from 'Urwah bin al-Zubayr via his son Hisham is one of the most reliable family chains in early Islam, directly attesting a consonantal substitution ('awthanan' vs 'inathan') in Aisha's personal Mushaf.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10442- حدثنا سفيان قال، حدثنا أبو أسامة، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: كان في مصحف عائشة: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أَوْثَانًا ). قال أبو جعفر: روي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرؤها: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أُثُنًا ) بمعنى جمع "وثن".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10442 - Sufyan narrated to us, saying: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: In the Mushaf of 'A'ishah it was (written): (They only call on idols instead of Him). Abu Ja'far said: It was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: (They only call on [uthunan] instead of Him), in the meaning of the plural of 'wathan' (idol).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كان في مصحف عائشة: ( إِنْ يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِلا أَوْثَانًا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the Mushaf of 'A'ishah it was (written): (They only call on idols instead of Him).

uthmanic_arabic: وَإِن مِّنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ إِلَّا لَيُؤۡمِنَنَّ بِهِۦ قَبۡلَ مَوۡتِهِۦۖ وَيَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكُونُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ شَهِيدٗا
uthmanic_english: Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in it before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them.

variants.short_title: 'Before Their Death' vs 'Before His Death' in 4:159
variants.plain_english_hook: Does 4:159 mean every Jew and Christian will believe in Jesus before 'his' (that person's or Jesus's) death? Ubayy bin Kab's reading had the plural 'before their death'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:159 — 'Qabla Mawtihim' (Before Their Death) in Ubayy's Reading
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:159 (وَإِنْ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكِتَابِ إِلَّا لَيُؤْمِنَنَّ بِهِ قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ), the singular pronoun in 'before his death' (قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِ) generated a major exegetical split over whether the pronoun refers to Jesus (after his eschatological descent) or to every individual among the People of the Book at the moment of dying. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains (graded sahih by Ibn Kathir) that Ibn Abbas argued for the latter by citing the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: 'before their death' (قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِمْ).

variants.variant_target_english: before their death

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir prefer interpreting the Uthmanic singular pronoun 'before his death' as referring to Jesus's future death after his second coming, treating Ubayy's plural 'before their death' as reflecting the alternative interpretation.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir explicitly certifies that the chains to Ibn Abbas citing Ubayy bin Ka'b's reading 'qabla mawtihim' (with a final mim) are authentic (asanid sahiha), demonstrating how a single consonantal pronoun difference changes the verse from an eschatological prophecy about Jesus's return to a claim about every dying scripturalist.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10814- حدثنا محمد بن بشار قال، حدثنا عبد الرحمن قال، حدثنا سفيان، عن أبي حصين، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته "، قال: في قراءة أبيّ: ( قَبْلَ مَوْتِهِمْ ). 10814م- حدثني إسحاق بن إبراهيم بن حبيب بن الشهيد قال، حدثنا عتاب بن بشير، عن خصيف، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عباس: " وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته "، قال: هي في قراءة أبي: ( قبل موتهم ) ، ليس يهودي يموت أبدا حتى يؤمن بعيسى.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10814m - Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin al-Shahid narrated to me... from Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: {Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in it before his death.} He said: "It is in the recitation of Ubayy: (before their death), no Jew ever dies until he believes in 'Isa."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي في قراءة أبي: ( قبل موتهم )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of Ubayy: (before their death)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا عتاب بن بشير عن خصيف ، عن سعيد بن جبير ، عن ابن عباس : ( وإن من أهل الكتاب إلا ليؤمنن به قبل موته ) قال : هي في قراءة أبي : ( قبل موتهم ) ليس يهودي يموت أبدا حتى يؤمن بعيسى ... فهذه كلها أسانيد صحيحة إلى ابن عباس ، وكذا صح عن مجاهد ، وعكرمة ، ومحمد بن سيرين . وبه يقول الضحاك وجويبر ، والسدي ، وحكاه عن ابن عباس ، ونقل قراءة أبي بن كعب : " قبل موتهم " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: From Sa'id bin Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: > **{Yet (there is) not one of the People of the Book except that he will indeed believe in him before his death}** He said, "It is in the recitation of Ubayy: '(before their deaths).' No Jew ever dies until he believes in 'Isa."... All of these are authentic chains of narration to Ibn 'Abbas, and this is also authentic from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, and Muhammad bin Sirin. This is also the view of Ad-Dahhak, Juwaybir, and As-Suddi, who also related it from Ibn 'Abbas and mentioned the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b: "before their deaths."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هي في قراءة أبي : ( قبل موتهم )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: It is in the recitation of Ubayy: '(before their deaths).'

uthmanic_arabic: لَّـٰكِنِ ٱلرَّـٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ مِنۡهُمۡ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ وَمَآ أُنزِلَ مِن قَبۡلِكَۚ وَٱلۡمُقِيمِينَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَۚ وَٱلۡمُؤۡتُونَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ أُوْلَـٰٓئِكَ سَنُؤۡتِيهِمۡ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمًا
uthmanic_english: But the ones who are firm in knowledge among them – and the believers – believe in what has been sent down to you, and what has been sent down before you. And the ones who observe the prayer, and who give the alms, and who believe in God and the Last Day, those – We shall give them a great reward.

variants.short_title: Grammatical Case Shift in 4:162 (Al-Muqimuna)
variants.plain_english_hook: Surah 4:162 shifts mid-sentence from nominative plural nouns to the accusative 'wal-muqimina'; Aisha called it a scribal error, and Ibn Masud's codex read the nominative 'wal-muqimuna'.
variants.title: Surah An-Nisa 4:162 — Nominative 'Wal-Muqimuna' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 4:162, 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلَاةَ) is written in the accusative/oblique case with a ya' (-ina), surrounded before and after by nominative plurals ending in waw-nun (الرَّاسِخُونَ, وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ, وَالْمُؤْتُونَ). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it is written in the nominative with a waw (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلَاةَ), and al-Tabari transmits the famous report of Urwah asking Aisha about 4:162, 5:69, and 20:63, to which she replied: 'O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe; they erred in the writing.'
variants.uthmanic_target_english: And the ones who observe the prayer

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical grammarians and commentators explain the Uthmanic accusative 'wal-muqimina' either as an accusative of praise (mansub 'ala al-madh) or as conjoined to the genitive pronoun 'ka' ('what was sent down to you'), arguing that Ubayy bin Ka'b's codex agreed with the Uthmanic rasm.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves two direct chains (via Abu Mu'awiyah and Yahya bin Sa'id from Hisham bin 'Urwah from his father) in which Aisha attributes the case anomaly in 4:162 to scribal error, while Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf preserved the regular nominative consonantal form 'wal-muqimuna' (with waw).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 10835- حدثنا الحسين بن يحيى قال، أخبرنا الحسين بن الأسود قال، حدثنا يحيى بن آدم، عن أبي بكر بن عياش، عن هشام بن عروة، عن أبيه قال: سألت عائشة عن اللحن في القرآن، عن قوله: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئُونَ) [سورة المائدة: 69]، وعن قوله: (وَالْمُقِيمِينَ الصَّلاةَ وَالْمُؤْتُونَ الزَّكَاةَ)، وعن قوله: (إِنْ هَذَانِ لَسَاحِرَانِ) [سورة طه: 63]، فقالت: يا ابن أختي، هذا عمل الكاتب، أخطئوا في الكتاب. وذكر أن ذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود: (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 10835 - Al-Husayn bin Yahya narrated to us... from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the grammatical anomaly (lahn) in the Qur'an, concerning His saying: {Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians [al-Sabi'una]} [5:69], and concerning His saying: {And the ones who observe the prayer [wa-al-muqimina al-salah] and who give the alms [wa-al-mu'tuna al-zakah]}, and concerning His saying: {Indeed, these two [in hadhani] are magicians} [20:63], and she said: O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe, they erred in the writing. And it is mentioned that it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (wa-al-muqimuna al-salah).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود: (وَالْمُقِيمُونَ الصَّلاةَ)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (wa-al-muqimuna al-salah)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقوله : ( والمقيمين الصلاة ) هكذا هو في جميع المصاحف الأئمة ، وكذا هو في مصحف أبي بن كعب . وذكر ابن جرير أنها في مصحف ابن مسعود : " والمقيمون الصلاة " ، قال : والصحيح قراءة الجميع . ثم رد على من زعم أن ذلك من غلط الكتاب ثم ذكر اختلاف الناس فقال بعضهم : هو منصوب على المدح .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: *(Wal-Muqimina As-Salah)* is written as such in all the leading copies of the Qur'an *(Masahif Al-A'immah)*, and similarly in the Mushaf of Ubayy bin Ka'b. Ibn Jarir mentioned that in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "and the ones who observe the prayer *(Wal-Muqimuna As-Salah)*." He said: "And the correct recitation is that of the majority." Then he refuted those who claimed that this was a mistake by the scribes.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في مصحف ابن مسعود : " والمقيمون الصلاة "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud it is: "and the ones who observe the prayer *(Wal-Muqimuna As-Salah)*."

variants.hadith_english: 10835 - Al-Husayn bin Yahya narrated to us... from Hisham bin 'Urwah, from his father, who said: I asked 'A'ishah about the grammatical anomaly (lahn) in the Qur'an, concerning His saying: {Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews and the Sabians [al-Sabi'una]} [5:69], and concerning His saying: {And the ones who observe the prayer [wa-al-muqimina al-salah] and who give the alms [wa-al-mu'tuna al-zakah]}, and concerning His saying: {Indeed, these two [in hadhani] are magicians} [20:63], and she said: O son of my sister, this is the work of the scribe, they erred in the writing. And it is mentioned that it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: 'and the ones who observe the prayer' (wa-al-muqimuna al-salah).

uthmanic_arabic: وَٱلسَّارِقُ وَٱلسَّارِقَةُ فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا جَزَآءَۢ بِمَا كَسَبَا نَكَٰلٗا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٞ
uthmanic_english: (As for) the male thief and the female thief: cut off their hands as a penalty for what they have done – a punishment from God. God is mighty, wise.

variants.short_title: 5:38 — Cut Off the Thief's 'Right Hands' vs. 'Hands'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran commands to 'cut off their hands' for theft, Abdullah bin Mas'ud's codex explicitly specified 'cut off their right hands.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'Their Right Hands' (Aymānahumā) for 'Their Hands' in 5:38
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 5:38, the Uthmanic text prescribes the punishment for theft as 'فَٱقۡطَعُوٓاْ أَيۡدِيَهُمَا' ('cut off their hands'). Both al-Tabari (11907–11910) and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'فَاقْطَعُوا أَيْمَانَهُمَا' ('cut off their right hands'), which Ibn Kathir classifies as an anomalous (shādhdh) recitation whose legal ruling is nevertheless unanimously followed by Islamic jurists.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: cut off their hands
variants.variant_target_english: cut off their right hands

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Ibn Kathir and Sunni legal theorists state that Ibn Mas'ud's wording is a non-canonical (shādhdh) explanatory reading, arguing that the restriction of amputation to the right hand is established by Prophetic practice rather than this variant text.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari records multiple Kufan transmissions from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and al-Sha'bi citing 'in our recitation / in the recitation of Abdullah: cut off their right hands' as a direct textual reading of the verse.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 11910 - حدثنا ابن وكيع قال، حدثنا أبي، عن سفيان، عن جابر، عن عامر قال: في قراءة عبد الله: ( والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **11910** - *Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Jabir, from 'Amir, who said:* In the recitation of 'Abdullah: *(The male thief and the female thief, so cut off their right hands)*.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله: ( والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah: *(The male thief and the female thief, so cut off their right hands)*

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: يقول تعالى حاكما وآمرا بقطع يد السارق والسارقة ، وروى الثوري عن جابر بن يزيد الجعفي عن عامر بن شراحيل الشعبي أن ابن مسعود كان يقرؤها : " والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما " . وهذه قراءة شاذة ، وإن كان الحكم عند جميع العلماء موافقا لها ، لا بها ، بل هو مستفاد من دليل آخر . وقد كان القطع معمولا به في الجاهلية ، فقرر في الإسلام وزيدت شروط أخر ، كما سنذكره إن شاء الله تعالى ، كما كانت القسامة والدية والقراض وغير ذلك من الأشياء التي ورد الشرع بتقريرها على ما كانت عليه ، وزيادات هي من تمام المصالح . ويقال : إن أول من قطع الأيدي في الجاهلية قريش قطعوا رجلا يقال له : " دويك " مولى لبني مليح بن عمرو من خزاعة كان قد سرق كنز الكعبة ، ويقال : سرقه قوم فوضعوه عنده .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Allah commands and decrees that the hand of the thief, male or female be cut off. Ath-Thawri reported from Jabir bin Yazid Al-Ju'fi from 'Amir bin Sharahil Ash-Sha'bi that Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands." This is a *Shaadh* (anomalous) recitation, although the ruling among all scholars is in agreement with it (cutting the right hand), not because of this recitation, but derived from another evidence.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: أن ابن مسعود كان يقرؤها : " والسارق والسارقة فاقطعوا أيمانهما "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn Mas'ud used to recite it: "And the male thief and the female thief, cut off their right hands."

uthmanic_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمۡ هُزُوٗا وَلَعِبٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَٱلۡكُفَّارَ أَوۡلِيَآءَۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
uthmanic_english: You who believe! Do not take those who take your religion in mockery and jest as allies, (either) from those who were given the Book before you, or (from) the disbelievers. Guard (yourselves) against God, if you are believers.

variants.short_title: 'Those Who Commit Shirk' vs 'The Disbelievers' (5:57)
variants.plain_english_hook: In 5:57, the standard Quran pairs 'those given the Book' with 'the disbelievers' (wal-kuffar); Ibn Masud's reading had 'and from those who associate partners with God'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:57 — 'Wa-mina Alladhina Ashraku' vs Uthmanic 'Wal-Kuffara'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 5:57, believers are forbidden to take mocking allies 'from those who were given the Book before you, or (from) the disbelievers [وَالْكُفَّارَ]', where reciters differed on whether وَالْكُفَّارَ is accusative or genitive since the preposition مِنْ ('from') is not repeated. Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'and from those who associate partners with God' (وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا), while Ubayy bin Ka'b recited 'and from the disbelievers' (وَمِنَ الْكُفَّارِ), both repeating the preposition مِنْ.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: or (from) the disbelievers
variants.variant_target_english: or from those who associate (partners with God)
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَتَّخِذُواْ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّخَذُواْ دِينَكُمۡ هُزُوٗا وَلَعِبٗا مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ وَٱلۡكُفَّارَ أَوۡلِيَآءَۚ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ

variants.variant_full_english: You who believe! Do not take those who take your religion in mockery and jest as allies, (either) from those who were given the Book before you, or from those who associate (partners with God). Guard (yourselves) against God, if you are believers.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite the recitations of Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy to show that 'al-kuffar' in 5:57 specifically denotes the Arab polytheists (al-mushrikun) as distinct from the People of the Book.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both Ibn Mas'ud's wording ('wa-mina alladhina ashraku') and Ubayy's wording ('wa-mina al-kuffari') supply the repeated preposition 'min' whose absence in the Uthmanic rasm caused a canonical grammatical dispute between the genitive and accusative readings of 'wal-kuffar'.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 12217 - حدثني به أحمد بن يوسف قال، حدثنا القاسم بن سلام قال، حدثنا حجاج، عن هارون، عن ابن مسعود= يقرأ: ( مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا ). وكذلك ذلك في قراءة أبيّ بن كعب فيما بلغنا: ( من الذين أوتوا الكتاب من قبلكم ومن الكفار أولياء ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 12217 - Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated to me, saying: al-Qasim bin Sallam narrated to us, saying: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, from Ibn Mas'ud, used to recite: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from those who commit shirk [polytheism]}. And likewise is that [found] in the recitation of Ubayy bin Ka'b, according to what has reached us: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from the disbelievers, as allies}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: عن ابن مسعود= يقرأ: ( مِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْكِتَابَ مِنْ قَبْلِكُمْ وَمِنَ الَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Ibn Mas'ud, used to recite: {from those who were given the Book before you, and from those who commit shirk [polytheism]}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: والمراد بالكفار ههنا المشركون ، وكذا وقع في قراءة ابن مسعود فيها ، رواه ابن جرير .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The meaning here of "the disbelievers" is the idolaters. Similarly, Ibn Jarir recorded that in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud [in place of "the disbelievers"] he recited it: "and those who commit *Shirk*."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: والمراد بالكفار ههنا المشركون ، وكذا وقع في قراءة ابن مسعود فيها ، رواه ابن جرير
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud [in place of "the disbelievers"] he recited it: "and those who commit *Shirk*."

uthmanic_arabic: لَا يُؤَاخِذُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِٱللَّغۡوِ فِيٓ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ وَلَٰكِن يُؤَاخِذُكُم بِمَا عَقَّدتُّمُ ٱلۡأَيۡمَٰنَۖ فَكَفَّـٰرَتُهُۥٓ إِطۡعَامُ عَشَرَةِ مَسَٰكِينَ مِنۡ أَوۡسَطِ مَا تُطۡعِمُونَ أَهۡلِيكُمۡ أَوۡ كِسۡوَتُهُمۡ أَوۡ تَحۡرِيرُ رَقَبَةٖۖ فَمَن لَّمۡ يَجِدۡ فَصِيَامُ ثَلَٰثَةِ أَيَّامٖۚ ذَٰلِكَ كَفَّـٰرَةُ أَيۡمَٰنِكُمۡ إِذَا حَلَفۡتُمۡۚ وَٱحۡفَظُوٓاْ أَيۡمَٰنَكُمۡۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يُبَيِّنُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
uthmanic_english: God will not take you to task for a slip in your oaths, but He will take you to task for what you have pledged by oath. Atonement for it is the feeding of ten poor persons with the average (amount of food) which you feed your households, or clothing them, or the setting free of a slave. Whoever does not find (the means to do that), (the penalty is) a fast for three days. That is the atonement for your oaths when you have sworn (them, and broken them). But guard your oaths! In this way God makes clear to you His signs, so that you may be thankful.

variants.short_title: Oath Atonement: 'Three Consecutive Days'
variants.plain_english_hook: The standard Quran requires fasting 'three days' to break an oath, leaving jurists divided on whether they must be back-to-back; Ibn Masud and Ubayy's codices explicitly added 'consecutive'.
variants.title: Surah Al-Ma'idah 5:89 — Addition of 'Mutatabi'at' (Consecutive) in Oath Expiation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 5:89, the expiation for a broken oath when unable to feed or clothe the poor is 'a fast for three days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple authentic chains that the codices and recitations of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b read 'a fast for three consecutive days' (فَصِيَامُ ثَلَاثَةِ أَيَّامٍ مُتَتَابِعَاتٍ), a variant that directly shaped Hanafi and Hanbali law requiring uninterrupted fasting.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: a fast for three days
variants.variant_target_english: a fast for three consecutive days

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical jurists and commentators classify the word 'mutatabi'at' (consecutive) either as an explanatory gloss (qira'a tafsiriyya) inserted by Companions or as a recitation whose wording was abrogated while its legal ruling remained debated.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 9750 - حدثنا عبد الأعلى بن واصل الأسدي، قال: ثنا عبيد الله بن موسى، عن أبي جعفر الرازي، عن الربيع بن أنس، عن أبي العالية، عن أبي بن كعب، أنه كان يقرأ: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". 9751 - حدثنا ابن وكيع، قال: ثنا يزيد بن هارون، عن قزعة بن سويد، عن سيف بن سليمان، عن مجاهد، قال: في قراءة عبد الله: "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات". فأما ما روي عن أبي وابن مسعود من قراءتهما "فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات" فذلك خلاف ما في مصاحفنا، وغير جائز لنا أن نشهد بشيء ليس في مصاحفنا من الكلام أنه من كتاب الله.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 9750 - 'Abd al-A'la b. Wasil al-Asadi narrated to us... from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy b. Ka'b, that he used to read: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. 9751 - Ibn Waki' narrated to us... from Mujahid, he said: In the reading of 'Abd Allah: 'a fast for three consecutive days'. As for what was narrated from Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud regarding their reading 'a fast for three consecutive days', that is contrary to what is in our manuscripts of the Qur'an.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال أبو جعفر الرازي ، عن الربيع ، عن أبي العالية ، عن أبي بن كعب أنه كان يقرؤها : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وحكاها مجاهد والشعبي وأبو إسحاق ، عن عبد الله بن مسعود . وقال إبراهيم : في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " فصيام ثلاثة أيام متتابعات " . وقال الأعمش : كان أصحاب ابن مسعود يقرءونها كذلك .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Abu Ja'far Ar-Razi recorded from Ar-Rabi', from Abu Al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy bin Ka'b that he used to read it as: 'Then he should fast three consecutive days.' Mujahid, Ash-Sha'bi, and Abu Ishaq narrated it from 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud. Ibrahim said: 'In the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Then he should fast three consecutive days."' Al-A'mash said: 'The companions of Ibn Mas'ud used to read it like that.'

uthmanic_arabic: وَكَذَٰلِكَ نُصَرِّفُ ٱلۡأٓيَٰتِ وَلِيَقُولُواْ دَرَسۡتَ وَلِنُبَيِّنَهُۥ لِقَوۡمٖ يَعۡلَمُونَ
uthmanic_english: In this way We vary the signs, so that they will say, ‘You have studied,’ and that We may make it clear to a people who know.

variants.short_title: 'He Has Studied' (Darasa) vs 'You Have Studied' (6:105)
variants.plain_english_hook: In 6:105, the standard Quran has 'so that they will say, You have studied' (darasta, with a final t); the codices of Ubayy and Ibn Masud read 'He has studied' (darasa).
variants.title: Surah Al-An'am 6:105 — 'Wa-li-Yaqulu Darasa' in Ubayy and Ibn Mas'ud's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 6:105, the consonantal rasm دَرَسْتَ (with a final ta') is read by the majority as 'You have studied' (darasta), by Ibn Kathir/Abu 'Amr as 'You have studied with others' (darasta, adding an alif), and by Ibn 'Amir as 'They have become old/erased' (darasat). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim bin Sallam and Ma'mar from Qatadah that in the codex/harf of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Abdullah bin Mas'ud the word was written without the final ta': 'so that they will say, He has studied' (وَلِيَقُولُوا دَرَسَ).

variants.variant_target_english: so that they will say, ‘He has studied,’

variants.variant_full_english: In this way We vary the signs, so that they will say, ‘He has studied,’ and that We may make it clear to a people who know.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari remarks that third-person 'darasa' and second-person 'darasta' both convey the disbelievers' allegation that the Prophet studied previous texts, while preferring 'darasta' because it conforms to the Uthmanic consonantal script.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: The absence of the final consonant ta' in 'darasa' is attested by both Qatadah and Abu 'Ubayd for the codices (harf) of both Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy bin Ka'b, representing a genuine consonantal divergence from the Uthmanic rasm.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 13730- حدثنا محمد بن عبد الأعلى قال، حدثنا محمد بن ثور, عن معمر قال، قال قتادة: " درست "، قرئت = وفي حرف ابن مسعود: " درس" . 13735- حدثني أحمد بن يوسف الثعلبي قال، حدثنا أبو عبيدة قال، حدثنا حجاج, عن هارون قال: هي في حرف أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود: " وليقولوا درس"، قال: يعني النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، قرأ .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 13730 - Muhammad bin 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us... from Qatadah: "darasat" means it was read = and in the reading [harf] of Ibn Mas'ud: "darasa" (he studied). 13735 - Ahmad bin Yusuf al-Tha'labi narrated to me... from Harun, who said: It is in the reading [harf] of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud: "so that they will say, darasa (he has studied)," meaning the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, read.

tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the reading [harf] of Ubayy bin Ka'b and Ibn Mas'ud: "so that they will say, darasa (he has studied),"

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال معمر ، عن قتادة : " درست " : قرئت . وفي حرف ابن مسعود " درس " وقال أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام : حدثنا حجاج ، عن هارون قال : هي في حرف أبي بن كعب وابن مسعود : " وليقولوا درس " قال : يعنون النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه قرأ .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ma'mar reported that Qatadah said: "' *darasat* ': it was read." And in the reading of Ibn Mas'ud it is ' *darasa* '. He said: They mean the Prophet (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), that he read."

uthmanic_english: The assembly of the people of Pharaoh said, ‘Will you leave Moses and his people to foment corruption on the earth and to forsake you and your gods?’ He said, ‘We shall kill their sons and keep their women alive. Surely we shall be supreme over them!’

variants.short_title: 7:127 — 'When They Have Forsaken You Not to Serve You'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where Pharaoh's chiefs ask if he will leave Moses 'to forsake you and your gods,' Ubayy bin Ka'b's codex read 'when they have forsaken you so as not to serve you and your gods.'
variants.title: Substitution of 'When They Have Forsaken You Not to Worship You' in 7:127
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 7:127, the Uthmanic text quotes Pharaoh's chiefs asking: 'أَتَذَرُ مُوسَىٰ وَقَوۡمَهُۥ لِيُفۡسِدُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَيَذَرَكَ وَءَالِهَتَكَۚ' ('Will you leave Moses and his people to foment corruption on the earth and to forsake you and your gods?'). Both al-Tabari (14961) and Ibn Kathir record via Harun bin Musa that in the reading (ḥarf) of Ubayy bin Ka'b this clause read 'وَقَدْ تَرَكُوكَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوكَ وَآلِهَتَكَ' ('when they have forsaken you so as not to serve you and your gods').

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari cites Ubayy's reading as an explanatory confirmation that the subjunctive verb 'wa-yadharaka' in the Uthmanic text is governed by syntactic diversion (ṣarf / circumstantial state) meaning 'while he has already forsaken worshipping you.'

variants.short_title: Missing Object Pronoun 'Annahum' in 8:59
variants.plain_english_hook: Al-Tabari criticizes the standard Hafs reading of 8:59 as grammatically incomplete unless 'annahum' ('that they') is present—as it was in Abdullah bin Masud's codex.
variants.title: Surah Al-Anfal 8:59 — 'Annahum Sabaqu' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs Uthmanic 'Sabaqu'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 8:59, the Kufan and Medinan reading (including Hafs) is وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ ('Do not let those who disbelieve think they have gotten away. Surely they will not escape'). Al-Tabari argues that reading third-person 'yahsabanna' with 'innahum' (kasra) is grammatically defective in Arabic because the verb 'yahsabu' requires two accusative objects, and explains that those reciters were influenced by the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud, which explicitly included the word أَنَّهُمْ ('that they'): وَلَا يَحْسَبَنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا أَنَّهُمْ سَبَقُوا إِنَّهُمْ لَا يُعْجِزُونَ.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians defending the Hafs reading argue either that 'annahum' is implicitly elided (mudmar) before 'sabaqu' or that 'sabaqu' functions in the sense of a participial second object ('sabiqin').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly declares the Hafs/Kufan reading 'non-praiseworthy' (ghayr mahmudah) and distant from eloquent Arabic speech unless 'annahum' is present in the text as it was in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ذلك بعض قرأة أهل المدينة والكوفة: " ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا "، بالياء في " يحسبن "، وكسر الألف من " إنهم ". وهي قراءة غير محمودة، لعلتين: إحداهما، خروجها عن قراءة القرأة وشذوذها عنها; والأخرى، بعدها عن الفصيح من كلام العرب. وأحسب أن الذي دعاه إلى ذلك، الاعتبار بقراءة عبد الله. وذلك أنه فيما ذكر في مصحف عبد الله: " ولا يحسبن الذين كفروا أنهم سبقوا إنهم لا يعجزون "، وهذا فصيح صحيح، إذا أدخلت " أنهم " في الكلام, لأن " يحسبن " عاملة في " أنهم ", وإذا لم يكن في الكلام " أنهم " كانت خالية من اسم تعمل فيه.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And some of the reciters of Al-Madinah and Al-Kufah recited it: "Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru," with a Ya' in "yahsabanna", and a Kasrah on the Alif of "innahum". And it is a non-praiseworthy recitation, for two reasons: one of them is its departure from the recitation of the reciters and its anomaly from it; and the other: its distance from the eloquent speech of the Arabs... And I suppose that what called him to that was the consideration of the recitation of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]. And that is because it is as was mentioned in the Mushaf of 'Abdullah: "Do not let those who disbelieve think that they [annahum] have gotten away; surely they will not escape" (Wa la yahsabanna alladhina kafaru annahum sabaqu innahum la yu'jizun), and this is eloquent and sound if "annahum" is inserted into the speech, because "yahsabanna" governs "annahum", and if "annahum" is not in the speech, it is devoid of a noun in which to operate.

uthmanic_english: Is it not a fact that they cover their hearts to hide from Him? Is it not (a fact) that (even) when they cover themselves with their clothing, He knows what they keep secret and what they speak aloud? Surely He knows what is in the hearts.

variants.short_title: Ibn Abbas Reads 'Their Chests Fold Up' in Q. 11:5
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of 'they fold their chests' (yathnuna sudurahum), Ibn Abbas recited 'their chests fold up' (tathnawni suduruhum), adding an extra consonant and changing the grammatical subject.
variants.title: Morphological Shift to 'Tathnawni Suduruhum' in Q. 11:5 (Recitation of Ibn Abbas)
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4681 and 4682, Tafsir al-Tabari, and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn 'Abbas recited Q. 11:5 as 'أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ' (*tathnawnī ṣudūruhum*, on the rare verbal pattern *taf'aw'il* with *ṣudūruhum* in the nominative case as the subject: 'their chests fold up / bend over') instead of the Uthmanic 'أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ يَثۡنُونَ صُدُورَهُمۡ' (*yathnūna ṣudūrahum*, with *ṣudūrahum* in the accusative as the object: 'they fold/cover their chests'). This variant alters both the consonantal skeleton (prefixing *tā'* and adding a final *yā'*) and the syntax of the clause.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir explain that 'tathnawni' is an intensive Arabic morphological pattern (taf'aw'il) close in meaning to the standard reading, though al-Tabari declares the Uthmanic reading 'yathnuna' obligatory due to the consensus of the garrison cities.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn 'Abbas's reading 'tathnawni suduruhum' is attested by multiple independent chains in Sahih al-Bukhari (4681, 4682) and Tafsir al-Tabari (17951–17954) and cannot be accommodated by the standard Uthmanic consonantal rasm ('يثنون').

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا الْحَسَنُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ صَبَّاحٍ، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجٌ، قَالَ قَالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ أَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}‏ قَالَ سَأَلْتُهُ عَنْهَا فَقَالَ أُنَاسٌ كَانُوا يَسْتَحْيُونَ أَنْ يَتَخَلَّوْا فَيُفْضُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ، وَأَنْ يُجَامِعُوا نِسَاءَهُمْ فَيُفْضُوا إِلَى السَّمَاءِ، فَنَزَلَ ذَلِكَ فِيهِمْ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Muhammad bin `Abbas bin Ja`far:That he heard Ibn `Abbas reciting: "No doubt! They fold up their breasts." (11.5) and asked him about its explanation. He said, "Some people used to hide themselves while answering the call of nature in an open space lest they be exposed to the sky, and also when they had sexual relation with their wives in an open space lest they be exposed to the sky, so the above revelation was sent down regarding them

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنِي إِبْرَاهِيمُ بْنُ مُوسَى، أَخْبَرَنَا هِشَامٌ، عَنِ ابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ، وَأَخْبَرَنِي مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ عَبَّادِ بْنِ جَعْفَرٍ، أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَرَأَ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}‏ قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا الْعَبَّاسِ مَا تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ قَالَ كَانَ الرَّجُلُ يُجَامِعُ امْرَأَتَهُ فَيَسْتَحِي أَوْ يَتَخَلَّى فَيَسْتَحِي فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ‏}‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Muhammad bin `Abbas bin Ja`far:Ibn `Abbas recited. "No doubt! They fold up their breasts." I said, "O Abu `Abbas! What is meant by "They fold up their breasts?" He said, "A man used to feel shy on having sexual relation with his wife or on answering the call of nature (in an open space) so this Verse was revealed:-- "No doubt! They fold up their breasts
hadiths.highlight_arabic: أَنَّ ابْنَ عَبَّاسٍ، قَرَأَ ‏{‏أَلاَ إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ‏}
hadiths.highlight_english: Ibn `Abbas recited. "No doubt! They fold up their breasts."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ ذلك : ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ ) ، على مثال " تحلولي الثمرة "، " تفعوعل " ... قال أبو جعفر: والصواب من القراءة في ذلك عندنا ما عليه قراء الأمصار، وهو: ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ يَثْنُونَ صُدُورَهُمْ ) ، على مثال " يفعلون "، و " الصدور " نصب .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: {Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum} (Behold their breasts did fold up), on the pattern of "Tahlawli Al-Thamarah" (The fruit becomes sweet), "Taf'aw'il"... Abu Ja'far said: The correct recitation in that regard according to us is what the reciters in the cities agreed upon, and it is: {Ala innahum yathnuna sudurahum} on the pattern of "Yaf'alun" (they do), and "Al-Sudur" (hearts/chests) is accusative (Nasb).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه كان يقرأ ذلك : ( أَلا إِنَّهُمْ تَثْنَوْنِي صُدُورُهُمْ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite it: {Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum} (Behold their breasts did fold up)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقرأ ابن عباس : " ألا إنهم تثنوني صدورهم " ، برفع الصدور على الفاعلية ، وهو قريب المعنى .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn 'Abbas recited: "Ala innahum tathnawni suduruhum" (Is it not a fact that their breasts fold up), with 'breasts' (suduruhum) in the nominative case as the subject, and it is close in meaning.

uthmanic_english: They said, ‘Lot! Surely we are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife, (for) surely what is about to smite them is going to smite her. Surely their appointment is the morning. Is the morning not near?’

variants.short_title: 11:81 — Omitting 'Let None of You Turn Around'
variants.plain_english_hook: In the angels' command to Lot, Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife,' omitting 'and let none of you turn around.'
variants.title: Omission of 'And Let None of You Turn Around' Before 'Except Your Wife' in 11:81
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 11:81, the Uthmanic text reads 'فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ' ('So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife,'), creating a famous grammatical dispute over whether 'except your wife' modifies 'your family' or 'let none of you turn around.' Al-Tabari (18423) and Ibn Kathir record that in the reading (ḥarf) of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read 'فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ' ('So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife,'), omitting the intervening clause.
variants.uthmanic_target_arabic: فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَ
variants.uthmanic_target_english: So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife
variants.variant_target_arabic: فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلِ إِلَّا امْرَأَتَكَ
variants.variant_target_english: So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: قَالُواْ يَٰلُوطُ إِنَّا رُسُلُ رَبِّكَ لَن يَصِلُوٓاْ إِلَيۡكَۖ فَأَسۡرِ بِأَهۡلِكَ بِقِطۡعٖ مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ وَلَا يَلۡتَفِتۡ مِنكُمۡ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا ٱمۡرَأَتَكَۖ إِنَّهُۥ مُصِيبُهَا مَآ أَصَابَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ مَوۡعِدَهُمُ ٱلصُّبۡحُۚ أَلَيۡسَ ٱلصُّبۡحُ بِقَرِيبٖ
variants.uthmanic_full_english: They said, ‘Lot! Surely we are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. So journey with your family in a part of the night, and let none of you turn around, except your wife, (for) surely what is about to smite them is going to smite her. Surely their appointment is the morning. Is the morning not near?’

variants.variant_full_english: They said, ‘Lot! Surely we are messengers of your Lord. They will not reach you. So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife, (for) surely what is about to smite them is going to smite her. Surely their appointment is the morning. Is the morning not near?’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians and exegetes cite Ibn Mas'ud's reading as an interpretive reordering or abridged citation demonstrating why the majority of canonical readers place 'your wife' (imra'ataka) in the accusative case as an exception to 'your family.'
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari (18423) transmits this directly via Abu Ubayd al-Qasim bin Sallam as the reading (ḥarf) of Ibn Mas'ud, resolving the syntactic ambiguity in the Uthmanic text where the prohibition against turning around separates 'your family' from 'except your wife.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 18423- حدثني بذلك أحمد بن يوسف قال ، حدثنا القاسم بن سلام قال ، حدثنا حجاج، عن هارون، قال في حرف ابن مسعود: ( فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلَ إلا امْرَأَتَكَ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt:
**18423-** *Ahmad bin Yusuf narrated that to me, he said: Al-Qasim bin Sallam narrated to us, he said: Hajjaj narrated to us, from Harun, he said in the Harf (reading variant) of Ibn Mas'ud:* 
{So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في حرف ابن مسعود: ( فَأَسْرِ بِأَهْلِكَ بِقِطْعٍ مِنَ اللَّيْلَ إلا امْرَأَتَكَ)
tafsir_sources.highlight_english:
in the Harf (reading variant) of Ibn Mas'ud:* 
{So journey with your family in a part of the night, except your wife}

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: ( إلا امرأتك ) قال الأكثرون : هو استثناء من المثبت وهو قوله : ( فأسر بأهلك ) تقديره ( إلا امرأتك ) وكذلك قرأها ابن مسعود ونصب هؤلاء امرأتك; لأنه من مثبت ، فوجب نصبه عندهم .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Meaning, > {except your wife}. And likewise Ibn Mas'ud recited it, and these (scholars) read 'your wife' with Nasb (accusative case) because it is from an affirmative, so its Nasb is obligatory according to them.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: تقديره ( إلا امرأتك ) وكذلك قرأها ابن مسعود
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: Meaning, > {except your wife}. And likewise Ibn Mas'ud recited it

uthmanic_arabic: وَدَخَلَ مَعَهُ ٱلسِّجۡنَ فَتَيَانِۖ قَالَ أَحَدُهُمَآ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَعۡصِرُ خَمۡرٗاۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡأٓخَرُ إِنِّيٓ أَرَىٰنِيٓ أَحۡمِلُ فَوۡقَ رَأۡسِي خُبۡزٗا تَأۡكُلُ ٱلطَّيۡرُ مِنۡهُۖ نَبِّئۡنَا بِتَأۡوِيلِهِۦٓۖ إِنَّا نَرَىٰكَ مِنَ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
uthmanic_english: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) pressing wine,’ and the other said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Inform us about its interpretation. Surely we see you are one of the doers of good.’

variants.short_title: 'Pressing Grapes' vs 'Pressing Wine' in 12:36
variants.plain_english_hook: In Joseph's prison, the cupbearer says 'I saw myself pressing wine' in the standard Quran; in Abdullah bin Masud's recitation, he said 'pressing grapes'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:36 — 'A'siru 'Inaban' (Pressing Grapes) vs 'Khamran' (Wine)
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:36, Pharaoh's cupbearer tells Joseph in prison, 'Surely I saw myself (in a dream) pressing wine [خَمْرًا].' Because one physically presses grapes rather than finished wine, both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via multiple chains (through Muhammad bin al-Hanafiyyah and al-A'mash from Zayd bin Wahb) that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'Surely I saw myself pressing grapes [عِنَبًا]'.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: pressing wine
variants.variant_target_english: pressing grapes

One of them said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) pressing wine,’ and the other said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Inform us about its interpretation. Surely we see you are one of the doers of good.’

variants.variant_full_english: And two young men entered the prison with him. One of them said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) pressing grapes,’ and the other said, ‘Surely I saw myself (in a dream) carrying bread on my head, from which the birds were eating. Inform us about its interpretation. Surely we see you are one of the doers of good.’

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators explain the Uthmanic word 'khamran' (wine) either as rhetorical metonymy (calling raw grapes by what they will eventually become) or as a dialectal usage from Oman where grapes were reportedly called khamr.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Ibn Kathir cites a direct Kufan chain (Sharīk from al-A'mash from Zayd bin Wahb from Ibn Mas'ud) alongside al-Tabari's transmission proving that Ibn Mas'ud's codex read the literal noun 'inaban' (grapes) in place of 'khamran' (wine).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وعني بقوله: (أعصر خمرا) ، أي: إني أرى في نومي أني أعصر عنبا . وكذلك ذلك في قراءة ابن مسعود فيما ذكر عنه . 19273 - حدثنا ابن وكيع , قال: حدثنا أبي , عن أبي سلمة الصائغ , عن إبراهيم بن بشير الأنصاري , عن محمد بن الحنفية قال في قراءة ابن مسعود: " إني أراني أعصر عنبا".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: And He meant by His saying: {pressing wine (khamr)}, meaning: "I see in my sleep that I am pressing grapes ('inab)." And so it is in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud based on what was mentioned about him. 19273 — Ibn Waki' narrated to us, he said: My father narrated to us, from Abu Salamah Al-Sa'igh, from Ibrahim bin Bashir Al-Ansari, from Muhammad bin Al-Hanafiyyah who said [that it is] in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes ('inab)."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة ابن مسعود: " إني أراني أعصر عنبا"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes ('inab)."

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: فرأى الساقي أنه يعصر خمرا - يعني عنبا - وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إني أراني أعصر عنبا " . ورواه ابن أبي حاتم ، عن أحمد بن سنان ، عن يزيد بن هارون ، عن شريك ، عن الأعمش ، عن زيد بن وهب ، عن ابن مسعود : أنه قرأها : " أعصر عنبا " .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: The cupbearer saw that he was pressing wine - meaning grapes - and likewise it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes." Ibn Abi Hatim recorded it from Ahmad bin Sinan, from Yazid bin Harun, from Sharik, from Al-A'mash, from Zayd bin Wahb, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he recited it: "pressing grapes."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود : " إني أراني أعصر عنبا "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: "Surely I saw myself pressing grapes."

uthmanic_arabic: فَبَدَأَ بِأَوۡعِيَتِهِمۡ قَبۡلَ وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَخۡرَجَهَا مِن وِعَآءِ أَخِيهِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ كِدۡنَا لِيُوسُفَۖ مَا كَانَ لِيَأۡخُذَ أَخَاهُ فِي دِينِ ٱلۡمَلِكِ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ نَرۡفَعُ دَرَجَٰتٖ مَّن نَّشَآءُۗ وَفَوۡقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلۡمٍ عَلِيمٞ
uthmanic_english: So he began with their packs before (searching) his brother’s pack, (and) then he brought it out of his brother’s pack. In this way We plotted for (the sake of) Joseph. He was not one to take his brother, in (accord with) the religion of the king, unless God had (so) pleased. We raise in rank whomever We please, and above everyone who has knowledge is the One who knows.

variants.short_title: 'Above Every Knower' ('Alim vs Dhi 'Ilm) in 12:76
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran concludes 12:76 with 'and above everyone who has knowledge [dhi 'ilmin] is the One who knows', Ibn Masud's reading had 'above every knower ['alimin]'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:76 — 'Wa-Fawqa Kulli 'Alimin 'Alim' in Ibn Mas'ud's Recitation
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:76, the verse concludes وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ ذِي عِلْمٍ عَلِيمٌ ('and above everyone who has knowledge is the One who knows'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Qatadah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it read وَفَوْقَ كُلِّ عَالِمٍ عَلِيمٌ ('and above every knower is the One who knows'), replacing the two-word construct ذِي عِلْمٍ with the single active participle عَالِمٍ.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators view 'kulli 'alimin' (every knower) and 'kulli dhi 'ilmin' (everyone possessing knowledge) as synonymous expressions from the same root.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: While semantically close, the replacement of the two-word Uthmanic construct 'dhi 'ilmin' with the single participle ''alimin' is an unmistakable consonantal difference attested in both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 19608 - حدثنا بشر قال، حدثنا يزيد قال، حدثنا سعيد , عن قتادة , قوله: (وفوق كل ذي علم عليم) ، حتى ينتهي العلم إلى الله , منه بدئ , وتعلمت العلماء , وإليه يعود . في قراءة عبد الله: " وفوق كل عالم عليم".

uthmanic_arabic: فَلَمَّا دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ قَالُواْ يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ مَسَّنَا وَأَهۡلَنَا ٱلضُّرُّ وَجِئۡنَا بِبِضَٰعَةٖ مُّزۡجَىٰةٖ فَأَوۡفِ لَنَا ٱلۡكَيۡلَ وَتَصَدَّقۡ عَلَيۡنَآۖ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَجۡزِي ٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ
uthmanic_english: When they entered upon him, they said, ‘Great one! Hardship has touched us and our house, and we have brought merchandise of little value. Fill up the measure for us and be charitable to us. Surely God rewards the charitable.’

variants.short_title: 'Load Up Our Mounts' vs 'Fill Up the Measure' (12:88)
variants.plain_english_hook: When Joseph's brothers bring meager goods in 12:88, they ask him to 'fill up the measure for us' in the standard Quran; in Ibn Masud's codex, they said 'load up our mounts'.
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:88 — 'Fa-Awqir Rikabana' (Load Up Our Mounts) in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:88, Joseph's brothers say: 'we have brought merchandise of little value [مُزْجَاةٍ]. Fill up the measure for us [فَأَوْفِ لَنَا الْكَيْلَ] and be charitable to us.' Al-Tabari records through three independent chains to Ibrahim al-Nakha'i that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and the recitation of his disciples it read فَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا / وَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا ('Load up our mounts for us'), which Ibrahim cited to prove that 'muzjah' meant scanty in quantity rather than counterfeit.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars treat 'wa-awqir rikabana' (load up our mounts) as an explanatory reading conveying the practical meaning of 'fa-awfi lana al-kayla' (fill up the measure for us).
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves three separate Kufan chains from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i explicitly attesting that 'wa-awqir rikabana' was written in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and actively recited by his companions.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: 19754- حدثنا ابن حميد ، قال: حدثنا جرير ، عن مغيرة ، عن يزيد بن الوليد ، عن إبراهيم ، في قوله: ( وجئنا ببضاعة مزجاة ) ، قال: قليلة ، ألا تسمع إلى قوله: " فَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنَا " ، وهم يقرءون كذلك. 19755- حدثني يعقوب بن إبراهيم ، قال: حدثنا هشيم ، قال، أخبرنا مغيرة ، عن إبراهيم ، أنه قال: ما أراها إلا القليلة ، لأنها في مصحف عبد الله: " وَأَوْقِرْ رِكَابَنا " ، يعني قوله: " مزجاة ".
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: **19754** — *Ibn Humayd narrated to us, he said: Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Yazid b. al-Walid, from Ibrahim, regarding His saying:* {and we have brought merchandise of little value [muzjah]}, he said: "Meager, do you not hear His saying: 'And fill up our mounts' [fa'awqir rikābanā], and they recite it thus." **19755** — *Ya'qub b. Ibrahim narrated to me, he said: Hushaym narrated to us, he said: Mughirah informed us, from Ibrahim, that he said:* "I do not consider it to be other than 'meager', because it is in the codex of 'Abdullah [Ibn Mas'ud]: 'And fill up our mounts' [wa'awqir rikābanā], meaning His saying: 'of little value' [muzjah]."

uthmanic_arabic: وَكَأَيِّن مِّنۡ ءَايَةٖ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيۡهَا وَهُمۡ عَنۡهَا مُعۡرِضُونَ
uthmanic_english: How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by! Yet they turn away from it.

variants.short_title: 'Walk Upon Them' vs 'Pass By Them' in 12:105
variants.plain_english_hook: In 12:105, the standard Quran asks how many signs in the heavens and earth people 'pass by' (yamurruna); in Abdullah bin Masud's codex, it read 'walk upon' (yamshuna).
variants.title: Surah Yusuf 12:105 — 'Yamshuna 'Alayha' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf vs 'Yamurruna'
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 12:105, the verse reads وَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ آيَةٍ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ يَمُرُّونَ عَلَيْهَا ('How many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by!'). Al-Tabari records via Qatadah that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud it was written يَمْشُونَ عَلَيْهَا ('do they walk upon!').

scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari preserves Qatadah's direct testimony that 'yamshuna 'alayha' (replacing the root m-r-r with m-sh-y) stood in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud.

uthmanic_arabic: وَقَدۡ مَكَرُواْ مَكۡرَهُمۡ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكۡرُهُمۡ وَإِن كَانَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لِتَزُولَ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
uthmanic_english: They schemed their scheme, but their scheme was known to God, even though their scheme was (such as) to remove the mountains by it.’

variants.short_title: 'Almost Removed Mountains' (Kada vs Kana) in 14:46
variants.plain_english_hook: Whether 14:46 means their plot 'could never' move mountains or 'almost' moved mountains depends on one letter: standard 'kana' (was) vs Ibn Masud, Ubayy, Umar, and Ali's 'kada' (almost).
variants.title: Surah Ibrahim 14:46 — 'Wa-In Kada Makruhum' in Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy's Codices
variants.diff_summary: In the Uthmanic text of 14:46, the clause وَإِنْ كَانَ مَكْرُهُمْ لِتَزُولَ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with nun in 'kana') is interpreted by the majority of reciters (who read 'litazula') as a negation: 'and their scheme was not such as to remove the mountains.' Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record that Abdullah bin Mas'ud (in his Mushaf), Ubayy bin Ka'b, Umar bin al-Khattab, and Ali bin Abi Talib read وَإِنْ كَادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الْجِبَالُ (with dal in 'kada' and dammah on 'latazulu'), reversing the sense to an affirmative near-occurrence: 'and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it.'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari acknowledges that Companions and Successors recited 'wa-in kada' with a dal, but rules that it is impermissible to recite it today because the Uthmanic manuscripts are written 'wa-in kana' with a nun, and one may not alter the orthography of the Muslims' Mushafs.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari's explicit concession—that the Companion reading 'wa-in kada' (attested for Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf, Umar, Ali, and Ubayy) is grammatically sound and was adapted by the canonical Kufan reciter al-Kisa'i onto the Uthmanic rasm 'wa-in kana latazulu'—demonstrates how a non-Uthmanic consonantal variant directly generated a canonical Qira'at dispute.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال ابن جريج: أخبرني عمرو بن دينار ، عن عكرمة ، عن عمر بن الخطاب ، أنه كان يقرأ " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". قال قتادة: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". وذلك أن الذين قرءوا ذلك بفتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية قرءوا: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ " بالدال ، وهي إذا قرئت كذلك ، فالصحيح من القراءة مع " وَإِنْ كادَ " فتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية على ما قرءوا ، وغير جائز عندنا القراءة كذلك ، لأن مصاحفنا بخلاف ذلك ، وإنما خطَّ مصاحفنا وإن كان بالنون لا بالدال.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Amr bin Dinar informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from 'Umar bin al-Khattab, that he used to recite: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. Qatadah said: And in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. And that is because those who recited it with a fathah on the first lam and a dammah on the second recited: '{wa-in kada makruhum}' with a dal... And it is not permissible in our view to recite like that, because our manuscripts are contrary to that. The script of our manuscripts is 'wa-in kana' with a nun, not with a dal.

tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the codex (Mushaf) of 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: قال : فهو قول الله - عز وجل - : " وإن كاد مكرهم لتزول منه الجبال " . قال أبو إسحاق : وكذلك هي في قراءة عبد الله : " وإن كاد مكرهم " . قلت : وكذا روي عن أبي بن كعب ، وعمر بن الخطاب - رضي الله عنهما - أنهما قرآ : " وإن كاد " كما قرأ علي .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is the saying of Allah (the Exalted and Most Honored): 'though their plot was almost (*Wa in kad*) one to remove the mountains from their places.' Abu Ishaq said: "And similarly it is in the recitation of 'Abdullah: '*Wa in kad makruhum*' (though their plot was almost...)." I (Ibn Kathir) say: And similarly it was narrated from Ubayy bin Ka'b and 'Umar bin Al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with them) that they recited "*Wa in kad*" as 'Ali recited.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله : " وإن كاد مكرهم "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: in the recitation of 'Abdullah: '*Wa in kad makruhum*'

variants.variant_arabic: وَقَدۡ مَكَرُواْ مَكۡرَهُمۡ وَعِندَ ٱللَّهِ مَكۡرُهُمۡ وَإِن كَادَ مَكۡرُهُمۡ لَتَزُولُ مِنۡهُ ٱلۡجِبَالُ
variants.variant_english: They schemed their scheme, but their scheme was known to God, and indeed their scheme almost removed the mountains by it.’
variants.hadith_arabic: قال ابن جريج: أخبرني عمرو بن دينار ، عن عكرمة ، عن عمر بن الخطاب ، أنه كان يقرأ " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". قال قتادة: وفي مصحف عبد الله بن مسعود: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ لَتَزُولُ مِنْهُ الجِبالُ ". وذلك أن الذين قرءوا ذلك بفتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية قرءوا: " وَإِنْ كادَ مَكْرُهُمْ " بالدال ، وهي إذا قرئت كذلك ، فالصحيح من القراءة مع " وَإِنْ كادَ " فتح اللام الأولى ورفع الثانية على ما قرءوا ، وغير جائز عندنا القراءة كذلك ، لأن مصاحفنا بخلاف ذلك ، وإنما خطَّ مصاحفنا وإن كان بالنون لا بالدال.
variants.hadith_english: Ibn Jurayj said: 'Amr bin Dinar informed me, from 'Ikrimah, from 'Umar bin al-Khattab, that he used to recite: '{And their plot almost caused the mountains to move from it}'. And that is because those who recited it with a fathah on the first lam and a dammah on the second recited: '{wa-in kada makruhum}' with a dal... And it is not permissible in our view to recite like that, because our manuscripts are contrary to that. The script of our manuscripts is 'wa-in kana' with a nun, not with a dal.

uthmanic_english: (It is incumbent) on God (to set the) direction of the way, yet (there is) deviation from it. If He had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.

variants.short_title: 16:9 — 'Among You Is One Who Deviates' vs. 'From It'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'there is deviation from it [the way],' Ibn Mas'ud's codex read 'and among you is one who deviates, and if God had pleased, He would have guided you.'

If He had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Qatadah that Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ لَهَدَاكُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ' ('yet among you is one who deviates. If God had (so) pleased, He would indeed have guided you all.'), shifting the subject of deviation from the paths ('minhā') to the human audience ('minkum') and adding the divine name 'Allāh.'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that whether deviation is attributed to the roads ('minhā,' i.e., deviant sects and paths) or to the people traveling them ('minkum,' i.e., those who stray from the truth), the underlying theological meaning remains consistent.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari transmits via two independent chains from Qatadah (through Sa'id bin Abi Arubah and Ma'mar) that Ibn Mas'ud's codex read both 'وَمِنْكُمْ جَائِرٌ' and the explicit subject 'وَلَوْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ.'
