uthmanic_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نُودِيَ لِلصَّلَوٰةِ مِن يَوۡمِ ٱلۡجُمُعَةِ فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ وَذَرُواْ ٱلۡبَيۡعَۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ خَيۡرٞ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
uthmanic_english: You who believe! When the call to prayer is made on the day of assembly, hurry to the remembrance of God, and leave business aside. That is better for you, if (only) you knew.

variants.short_title: 62:9 — 'Proceed' vs. 'Hurry' to Friday Prayer
variants.plain_english_hook: Instead of commanding believers to 'hurry' (fas'aw) to the Friday prayer, Umar bin al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud insisted until death that the verse reads 'proceed' (famḍū).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Proceed' (Famḍū) for 'Hurry' (Fas'aw) in 62:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 62:9, the Uthmanic text commands believers on Friday: 'فَٱسۡعَوۡاْ إِلَىٰ ذِكۡرِ ٱللَّهِ' ('hurry to the remembrance of God'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir document through numerous chains that Umar bin al-Khattab and Abdullah bin Mas'ud recited 'فَامْضُوا إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ' ('proceed to the remembrance of God'), with Ibn Mas'ud stating that had the verse read 'fas'aw' (hurry/run), he would have run until his cloak fell off.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: hurry to the remembrance of God

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators explain that 'fas'aw' in the Uthmanic text means 'intend and proceed with care' rather than physical running, citing the Prophetic hadith forbidding running to prayer, and view 'famḍū' as an abrogated reading or synonym.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Tabari's reports, when Umar was informed that Ubayy bin Ka'b recited 'fas'aw,' Umar replied that although Ubayy was the best reciter, the wording is 'famḍū,' and Ibn Umar testified that Umar never recited the verse any other way until he died.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثني يونس بن عبد الأعلى، قال: أخبرنا ابن وهب، قال: ثنا حنظلة بن أَبي سفيان الجمحّي، أنه سمع سالم بن عبد الله يحدّث عن أبيه، أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب يقرأ ( إذَا نُودِيَ لِلْصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الجُمْعَةِ فَامْضُوْاْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللهِ ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: (Proceed to the remembrance of God).
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: أنه سمع عمر بن الخطاب يقرأ ( إذَا نُودِيَ لِلْصَّلاةِ مِنْ يَوْمِ الجُمْعَةِ فَامْضُوْاْ إِلَى ذِكْرِ اللهِ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to recite it: (Proceed to the remembrance of God).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد أمر الله المؤمنين بالاجتماع لعبادته يوم الجمعة ، فقال : ( يا أيها الذين آمنوا إذا نودي للصلاة من يوم الجمعة فاسعوا إلى ذكر الله ) أي : اقصدوا واعمدوا واهتموا في مسيركم إليها ، وليس المراد بالسعي ها هنا المشي السريع ، وإنما هو الاهتمام بها ، كقوله تعالى : ( ومن أراد الآخرة وسعى لها سعيها وهو مؤمن ) [ الإسراء : 19 ] وكان عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما يقرآنها : " فامضوا إلى ذكر الله " . فأما المشي السريع إلى الصلاة فقد نهي عنه ، لما أخرجاه في الصحيحين ، عن أبي هريرة عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - قال : " إذا سمعتم الإقامة فامشوا إلى الصلاة ، وعليكم السكينة والوقار ، ولا تسرعوا ، فما أدركتم فصلوا ، وما فاتكم فأتموا " . لفظ البخاري
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with them - recited it: "Then proceed to the remembrance of Allah."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: وكان عمر بن الخطاب وابن مسعود رضي الله عنهما يقرآنها : " فامضوا إلى ذكر الله "
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab and Ibn Mas'ud - may Allah be pleased with them - recited it: "Then proceed to the remembrance of Allah."

uthmanic_arabic: يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقۡتُمُ ٱلنِّسَآءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ لِعِدَّتِهِنَّ وَأَحۡصُواْ ٱلۡعِدَّةَۖ وَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ رَبَّكُمۡۖ لَا تُخۡرِجُوهُنَّ مِنۢ بُيُوتِهِنَّ وَلَا يَخۡرُجۡنَ إِلَّآ أَن يَأۡتِينَ بِفَٰحِشَةٖ مُّبَيِّنَةٖۚ وَتِلۡكَ حُدُودُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَمَن يَتَعَدَّ حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ فَقَدۡ ظَلَمَ نَفۡسَهُۥۚ لَا تَدۡرِي لَعَلَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحۡدِثُ بَعۡدَ ذَٰلِكَ أَمۡرٗا
uthmanic_english: Prophet! When you divorce women, divorce them when they have reached (the end of) their waiting period. Count the waiting period, and guard (yourselves) against God your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor let them leave, unless they commit clear immorality. Those are the limits (set by) God. Whoever transgresses the limits (set by) God has done himself evil. You do not know, perhaps after that God may bring about a new situation.

variants.short_title: Reading 'At the Beginning Of' in Surah 65:1
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih Muslim 1471t and Tafsir al-Tabari, the Prophet, Ibn Abbas, and Ibn Umar recite Surah 65:1 as 'divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period' ('fi qubuli iddatihinna').
variants.title: Recitation of 'Fi Qubuli Iddatihinna' Instead of 'Li-Iddatihinna' in Surah 65:1
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'fa-ṭalliqūhunna li-'iddatihinna' ('divorce them when they have reached (the end of) their waiting period'), Sahih Muslim 1471t and multiple chains in Tafsir al-Tabari record that the Prophet, Ibn Abbas, and Abdullah bin Umar recited 'fa-ṭalliqūhunna fī qubuli 'iddatihinna' ('divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period'). This reading replaces the preposition 'li-' with the two-word prepositional phrase 'fī qubuli', specifying that a valid divorce must be initiated at the commencement of a woman's period of purity prior to marital relations.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical jurists and commentators explain that 'fī qubuli 'iddatihinna' was an explanatory recitation (qirā'ah tafsīriyyah) clarifying the intended legal meaning of the Uthmanic preposition 'li-'iddatihinna'.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih Muslim 1471t, Abdullah bin Umar explicitly states that the Prophet himself recited the verse as 'yā ayyuhā an-nabiyyu idhā ṭallaqtumu an-nisā'a fa-ṭalliqūhunna fī qubuli 'iddatihinna,' and al-Tabari records multiple chains of Ibn Abbas and Mujahid reciting this exact wording as scripture.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنِي هَارُونُ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا حَجَّاجُ بْنُ مُحَمَّدٍ، قَالَ قَالَ ابْنُ جُرَيْجٍ أَخْبَرَنِي أَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ، أَنَّهُ سَمِعَ عَبْدَ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنَ أَيْمَنَ، مَوْلَى عَزَّةَ يَسْأَلُ ابْنَ عُمَرَ وَأَبُو الزُّبَيْرِ يَسْمَعُ ذَلِكَ كَيْفَ تَرَى فِي رَجُلٍ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ حَائِضًا فَقَالَ طَلَّقَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ امْرَأَتَهُ وَهْىَ حَائِضٌ عَلَى عَهْدِ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَسَأَلَ عُمَرُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ إِنَّ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ بْنَ عُمَرَ طَلَّقَ امْرَأَتَهُ وَهْىَ حَائِضٌ ‏.‏ فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم ‏"‏ لِيُرَاجِعْهَا ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَرَدَّهَا وَقَالَ ‏"‏ إِذَا طَهَرَتْ فَلْيُطَلِّقْ أَوْ لِيُمْسِكْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ وَقَرَأَ النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَا أَيُّهَا النَّبِيُّ إِذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ فِي قُبُلِ عِدَّتِهِنَّ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Abu Zubair reported that he heard 'Abd al-Rahman b. Aiman (the freed slave of 'Azza) say that he asked Ibn 'Umar (Allah be pleased with them) and Abu Zubair heard:What is your opinion about the person who divorced his wife in the state of menses? Thereupon he said: Ibn Umar (Allah be pleased with them) divorced his wife during the lifetime of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) while she was in the state of menses. Upon this Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) told him to take her back and so he took her back and he (further) said: When she is pure, then either divorce her or retain her. Ibn 'Umar (Allah be pleased with them) said that Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) then recited this verse:" O Apostle, when you divorce women, divorce them at the commencement of their prescribed period" (Ixv)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: حدثنا ابن المثنى، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن عبد الله بن أبي نجيح، عن حميد الأعرج، عن مجاهد، أن رجلا سأل ابن عباس فقال: إنه طلق امرأته مئة، فقال: عصيت ربك، وبانت منك امرأتك، ولم تتق الله فيجعل لك مخرجًا، وقرأ هذه الآية: ( وَمَنْ يَتَّقِ اللَّهَ يَجْعَلْ لَهُ مَخْرَجًا ) ، وقال: ( يا أَيُّهَا الْنَّبِيُّ إذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ الْنِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ فِي قُبُلِ عِدَّتِهنَّ ) .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Ibn Al-Muthanna narrated to us, from Muhammad bin Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from 'Abdullah bin Abi Najih, from Humayd Al-A'raj, from Mujahid, that a man asked Ibn 'Abbas and said: Indeed, he divorced his wife a hundred times. He said: You have disobeyed your Lord, and your wife has become irrevocably separated from you. You did not guard yourself against God so that He could make a way out for you. And he recited this Ayah: {And whoever guards himself against God, He will make a way out for him}, and he said: {O Prophet! When you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: ( يا أَيُّهَا الْنَّبِيُّ إذَا طَلَّقْتُمُ الْنِّسَاءَ فَطَلِّقُوهُنَّ فِي قُبُلِ عِدَّتِهنَّ )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: {O Prophet! When you divorce women, divorce them at the beginning of their waiting period}

uthmanic_arabic: وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلۡأُنثَىٰٓ
uthmanic_english: By what created the male and the female!

variants.short_title: Omission of 'What Created' in Surah Al-Layl 92:3
variants.plain_english_hook: In eight Sahih Bukhari and Muslim narrations, Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda recited Surah 92:3 as 'By the male and the female,' omitting the Uthmanic words 'by what created.'
variants.title: Recitation of 'Wa-dh-Dhakari wa-l-Untha' Without 'Ma Khalaqa' in Surah 92:3
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf reads 'wa-mā khalaqa adh-dhakara wa-l-unthā' ('By what created the male and the female!'), the codex and recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud—corroborated by Abu Ad-Darda across six reports in Sahih al-Bukhari and two in Sahih Muslim—omitted the two words 'mā khalaqa' ('what created'), reading directly in the genitive oath: 'wa-dh-dhakari wa-l-unthā' ('By the male and the female!'). In these reports, Ibn Mas'ud's Kufan disciple Alqamah travels to Syria, where Abu Ad-Darda confirms that both he and Ibn Mas'ud learned the shorter reading directly from the Prophet's own lips.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars such as Ibn Kathir and Ibn Hajar state that while Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda heard this reading from the Prophet under the license of the seven ahruf, the majority of Companions followed the final presentation (al-'ardah al-akhirah) preserved in the Uthmanic Mushaf.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 3761, 4944, and Sahih Muslim 824a, Abu Ad-Darda swears by Allah after the Prophet's death that the Prophet taught him this exact wording 'mouth to mouth' (fāhu ilā fiyya) and declares regarding the Syrian Uthmanic reading: 'These people want me to recite wa-mā khalaqa, and I will not follow them.'

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ قَدِمَ أَصْحَابُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ فَطَلَبَهُمْ فَوَجَدَهُمْ فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ كُلُّنَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ يَحْفَظُ وَأَشَارُوا إِلَى عَلْقَمَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا، وَهَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونِي عَلَى أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim:The companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) came to Abu Darda', (and before they arrived at his home), he looked for them and found them. Then he asked them,: 'Who among you can recite (Qur'an) as `Abdullah recites it?" They replied, "All of us." He asked, "Who among you knows it by heart?" They pointed at 'Alqama. Then he asked Alqama. "How did you hear `Abdullah bin Mas`ud reciting Surat Al-Lail (The Night)?" Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them

hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو بَكْرِ بْنُ أَبِي شَيْبَةَ، وَأَبُو كُرَيْبٍ - وَاللَّفْظُ لأَبِي بَكْرٍ - قَالاَ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو مُعَاوِيَةَ عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ قَدِمْنَا الشَّامَ فَأَتَانَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ فَقَالَ أَفِيكُمْ أَحَدٌ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ فَقُلْتُ نَعَمْ أَنَا ‏.‏ قَالَ فَكَيْفَ سَمِعْتَ عَبْدَ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ هَذِهِ الآيَةَ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا وَاللَّهِ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا وَلَكِنْ هَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونَ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ وَمَا خَلَقَ ‏.‏ فَلاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Alqama reported. We went to Syria and Abu Darda' came to us and said:Is there anyone among you who recites according to the recitation of Abdullah? I said: Yes, it is I. He again said: How did you hear 'Abdullah reciting this verse: (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha = when the night covers)? He ('Alqama) said: I heard him reciting it (like this) (wa'l-lail-i-idha yaghsha) wa-dhakar wal untha = when the night covers and the males and the females). Upon this he said: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting in this way, but they (the Muslims of Syria) desire us to recite: (wa ma khalaqa), but I do not yield to their desire
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ سَمِعْتُهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: By Allah, I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting in this way, but they (the Muslims of Syria) desire us to recite: (wa ma khalaqa), but I do not yield to their desire

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مُوسَى، عَنْ أَبِي عَوَانَةَ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، دَخَلْتُ الشَّأْمَ فَصَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، فَقُلْتُ اللَّهُمَّ يَسِّرْ لِي جَلِيسًا‏.‏ فَرَأَيْتُ شَيْخًا مُقْبِلاً، فَلَمَّا دَنَا قُلْتُ أَرْجُو أَنْ يَكُونَ اسْتَجَابَ‏.‏ قَالَ مِنْ أَيْنَ أَنْتَ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ أَفَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ النَّعْلَيْنِ وَالْوِسَادِ وَالْمِطْهَرَةِ أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمُ الَّذِي أُجِيرَ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ أَوَلَمْ يَكُنْ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ السِّرِّ الَّذِي لاَ يَعْلَمُهُ غَيْرُهُ كَيْفَ قَرَأَ ابْنُ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ‏}‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا النَّبِيُّ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَاهُ إِلَى فِيَّ، فَمَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يَرُدُّونِي‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Alqama:I went to Sham and was offering a two-rak`at prayer; I said, "O Allah! Bless me with a (pious) companion." Then I saw an old man coming towards me, and when he came near I said, (to myself), "I hope Allah has given me my request." The man asked (me), "Where are you from?" I replied, "I am from the people of Kufa." He said, "Weren't there amongst you the Carrier of the (Prophet's) shoes, Siwak and the ablution water container? Weren't there amongst you the man who was given Allah's Refuge from the Satan? And weren't there amongst you the man who used to keep the (Prophet's) secrets which nobody else knew? How did Ibn Um `Abd (i.e. `Abdullah bin Mas`ud) use to recite Surat-al-lail (the Night:92)?" I recited:-- "By the Night as it envelops By the Day as it appears in brightness. And by male and female." (92.1- 3) On that, Abu Darda said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me read the Verse in this way after listening to him, but these people (of Sham) tried their best to let me say something different
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: On that, Abu Darda said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me read the Verse in this way after listening to him, but these people (of Sham) tried their best to let me say something different

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قَبِيصَةُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الشَّأْمَ فَسَمِعَ بِنَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ فَأَتَانَا فَقَالَ أَفِيكُمْ مَنْ يَقْرَأُ فَقُلْنَا نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ أَقْرَأُ فَأَشَارُوا إِلَىَّ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَنْتَ سَمِعْتَهَا مِنْ فِي صَاحِبِكَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ فِي النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهَؤُلاَءِ يَأْبَوْنَ عَلَيْنَا‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Alqama:I went to Sham with a group of the companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud). Abu Ad-Darda' heard of our arrival so he came to us and said, "Is there anybody among you who can recite (Qur'an)" We replied in the affirmative. Then he asked, "Who is the best reciter?" They pointed at me. Then he told me to recite, so I recited the verse:-- 'By the night as it envelops 'By the day as it appears in brightness; And by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, without 'wa-ma khalaqa'].' (92.1-3) Abu Ad-Darda' then said to me, "Did you hear it (like this) from the mouth of your friend (`Abdullah bin Mas`ud)?" I said, "Yes." He said, "I too, heard it (like this) from the mouth of the Prophet, but these people do not consider this recitation as the correct one
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: And by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, without 'wa-ma khalaqa']

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ حُجْرٍ السَّعْدِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ دَاوُدَ بْنِ أَبِي، هِنْدٍ عَنِ الشَّعْبِيِّ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ لَقِيتُ أَبَا الدَّرْدَاءِ فَقَالَ لِي مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ ‏.‏ قَالَ مِنْ أَيِّهِمْ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ ‏.‏ قَالَ هَلْ تَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَاقْرَأْ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَضَحِكَ ثُمَّ قَالَ هَكَذَا سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَؤُهَا ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Alqama reported:I met Abu Darda', and he said to me: To which country do you belong? I said: I am one of the people of Iraq. He again said: To which city? I replied: City of Kufa. He again said: Do you recite according to the recitation of 'Abdullah b. Mas'ud? I said: Yes. He said: Recite this verse (By the night when it covers) So I recited it: (By the night when it covers, and the day when it shines, and by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, omitting 'and He Who created']). He laughed and said: I have heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) reciting like this
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏ قَالَ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏ وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: and by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, omitting 'and He Who created']

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقد ذُكر عن عبد الله بن مسعود وأبي الدرداء: أنهما كانا يقرآن ذلك ( والذَّكَرِ والأنْثَى ) ويأثُرُه أبو الدرداء عن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. حدثنا محمد بن المثنى، قال: ثنا محمد بن جعفر، قال: ثنا شعبة، عن أبي إسحاق قال: في قراءة عبد الله ( وَاللَّيْلِ إذَا يَغْشَى والنَّهارِ إذَا تَجَلَّى والذَّكَر والأنْثَى ).
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: It has been mentioned regarding 'Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda': that they used to recite that as: {And the male and the female}, and Abu Ad-Darda' transmits it from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. ... In the recitation of 'Abdullah it is {By the night as it envelops, and the day as it appears, and the male and the female}.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: في قراءة عبد الله ( وَاللَّيْلِ إذَا يَغْشَى والنَّهارِ إذَا تَجَلَّى والذَّكَر والأنْثَى )
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: In the recitation of 'Abdullah it is {By the night as it envelops, and the day as it appears, and the male and the female}.

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء - وأما الجمهور فقرأوا ذلك كما هو مثبت في المصحف الإمام العثماني في سائر الآفاق : ( وما خلق الذكر والأنثى )
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet. However, the majority recited it as it is established in the 'Uthmani Mus-haf in all regions: {By what created the male and the female!}
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet.

variants.variant_arabic: وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
variants.variant_english: By the male and the female!
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عُمَرُ، حَدَّثَنَا أَبِي، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ قَدِمَ أَصْحَابُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَى أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ فَطَلَبَهُمْ فَوَجَدَهُمْ فَقَالَ أَيُّكُمْ يَقْرَأُ عَلَى قِرَاءَةِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ كُلُّنَا‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ يَحْفَظُ وَأَشَارُوا إِلَى عَلْقَمَةَ‏.‏ قَالَ كَيْفَ سَمِعْتَهُ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ عَلْقَمَةُ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَشْهَدُ أَنِّي سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ صلى الله عليه وسلم يَقْرَأُ هَكَذَا، وَهَؤُلاَءِ يُرِيدُونِي عَلَى أَنْ أَقْرَأَ ‏{‏وَمَا خَلَقَ الذَّكَرَ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏ وَاللَّهِ لاَ أُتَابِعُهُمْ‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim:The companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) came to Abu Darda', (and before they arrived at his home), he looked for them and found them. Then he asked them,: 'Who among you can recite (Qur'an) as `Abdullah recites it?" They replied, "All of us." He asked, "Who among you knows it by heart?" They pointed at 'Alqama. Then he asked Alqama. "How did you hear `Abdullah bin Mas`ud reciting Surat Al-Lail (The Night)?" Alqama recited: 'By the male and the female.' Abu Ad-Darda said, "I testify that I heard me Prophet reciting it likewise, but these people want me to recite it:-- 'And by Him Who created male and female.' but by Allah, I will not follow them

variants.short_title: Abu Ad-Darda's Refusal of 'Ma Khalaqa' in 92:3
variants.plain_english_hook: Abu Ad-Darda—the chief Quran teacher in Damascus—swore by Allah that Muhammad taught him Surah 92:3 as 'By the male and the female,' refusing Syrian pressure to add 'by what created.'
variants.title: Abu Ad-Darda's Sworn Testimony on Surah Al-Layl 92:3 Against the Syrian Mushaf
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih al-Bukhari (3742, 3743, 3761, 4943, 4944, 6278) and Sahih Muslim (824a, 824c), Abu Ad-Darda—appointed by Caliph Umar as the chief Quranic teacher of Damascus—questions Kufan visitors about how Abdullah bin Mas'ud recites Surah Al-Layl (92:1–3). When Alqamah recites 'wa-dh-dhakari wa-l-unthā' ('By the male and the female!') without the Uthmanic words 'mā khalaqa' ('what created'), Abu Ad-Darda testifies under oath: 'By Allah, the Prophet taught me to recite it thus, mouth to mouth, yet these people in Syria want me to recite wa-mā khalaqa—by Allah, I will not follow them!'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators argue that Abu Ad-Darda was defending the authenticity of the earlier harf he had personally learned from the Prophet before the Uthmanic standardization unified the community on a single reading.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Abu Ad-Darda's oath ('By Allah, I will not follow them!') shows that even in Damascus—one of the primary garrison cities receiving an official Uthmanic Mushaf—the resident Companion master reciter rejected the standardized wording in favor of the shorter prophetic reading he shared with Ibn Mas'ud.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا مَالِكُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ، حَدَّثَنَا إِسْرَائِيلُ، عَنِ الْمُغِيرَةِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ،، قَالَ قَدِمْتُ الشَّأْمَ فَصَلَّيْتُ رَكْعَتَيْنِ، ثُمَّ قُلْتُ اللَّهُمَّ يَسِّرْ لِي جَلِيسًا صَالِحًا، فَأَتَيْتُ قَوْمًا فَجَلَسْتُ إِلَيْهِمْ، فَإِذَا شَيْخٌ قَدْ جَاءَ حَتَّى جَلَسَ إِلَى جَنْبِي، قُلْتُ مَنْ هَذَا قَالُوا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ إِنِّي دَعَوْتُ اللَّهَ أَنْ يُيَسِّرَ لِي جَلِيسًا صَالِحًا فَيَسَّرَكَ لِي، قَالَ مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ قُلْتُ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ أَوَلَيْسَ عِنْدَكُمُ ابْنُ أُمِّ عَبْدٍ صَاحِبُ النَّعْلَيْنِ وَالْوِسَادِ وَالْمِطْهَرَةِ وَفِيكُمُ الَّذِي أَجَارَهُ اللَّهُ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ عَلَى لِسَانِ نَبِيِّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم أَوَلَيْسَ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ سِرِّ النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم الَّذِي لاَ يَعْلَمُ أَحَدٌ غَيْرُهُ ثُمَّ قَالَ كَيْفَ يَقْرَأُ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏، فَقَرَأْتُ عَلَيْهِ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ وَاللَّهِ لَقَدْ أَقْرَأَنِيهَا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنْ فِيهِ إِلَى فِيَّ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated 'Alqama:I went to Sham and offered a two-rak`at prayer and then said, "O Allah! Bless me with a good pious companion." So I went to some people and sat with them. An old man came and sat by my side. I asked, "Who is he?" They replied, "(He is) Abu-Ad-Darda.' I said (to him), "I prayed to Allah to bless me with a pious companion and He sent you to me." He asked me, "From where are you?" I replied, "From the people of Al-Kufa." He said, "Isn't there amongst you Ibn Um `Abd, the one who used to carry the shoes, the cushion(or pillow) and the water for ablution? Is there amongst you the one whom Allah gave Refuge from Satan through the request of His Prophet. Is there amongst you the one who keeps the secrets of the Prophet (ﷺ) which nobody knows except him?" Abu Darda further asked, "How does `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud) recite the Sura starting with, 'By the Night as it conceals (the light)." (92.1) Then I recited before him: 'By the Night as it envelops: And by the Day as it appears in brightness; And by male and female.' (91.1-3) On this Abu Ad-Darda' said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me recite the Sura in this way while I was listening to him (reciting it)
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏، فَقَرَأْتُ عَلَيْهِ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: On this Abu Ad-Darda' said, "By Allah, the Prophet (ﷺ) made me recite the Sura in this way while I was listening to him (reciting it)

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ جَعْفَرٍ، حَدَّثَنَا يَزِيدُ، عَنْ شُعْبَةَ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، أَنَّهُ قَدِمَ الشَّأْمَ‏.‏ وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو الْوَلِيدِ، حَدَّثَنَا شُعْبَةُ، عَنْ مُغِيرَةَ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، قَالَ ذَهَبَ عَلْقَمَةُ إِلَى الشَّأْمِ، فَأَتَى الْمَسْجِدَ فَصَلَّى رَكْعَتَيْنِ فَقَالَ اللَّهُمَّ ارْزُقْنِي جَلِيسًا‏.‏ فَقَعَدَ إِلَى أَبِي الدَّرْدَاءِ فَقَالَ مِمَّنْ أَنْتَ قَالَ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْكُوفَةِ‏.‏ قَالَ أَلَيْسَ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ السِّرِّ الَّذِي كَانَ لاَ يَعْلَمُهُ غَيْرُهُ ـ يَعْنِي حُذَيْفَةَ ـ أَلَيْسَ فِيكُمْ ـ أَوْ كَانَ فِيكُمُ ـ الَّذِي أَجَارَهُ اللَّهُ عَلَى لِسَانِ رَسُولِهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ ـ يَعْنِي عَمَّارًا ـ أَوَلَيْسَ فِيكُمْ صَاحِبُ السِّوَاكِ وَالْوِسَادِ ـ يَعْنِي ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ ـ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ يَقْرَأُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ فَقَالَ مَا زَالَ هَؤُلاَءِ حَتَّى كَادُوا يُشَكِّكُونِي، وَقَدْ سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibrahim:'Alaqama went to Sham and came to the mosque and offered a two-rak`at prayer, and invoked Allah: "O Allah! Bless me with a (pious) good companion." So he sat beside Abu Ad-Darda' who asked, "From where are you?" He said, "From the people of Kufa." Abu Darda' said, "Wasn't there among you the person who keeps the secrets (of the Prophet (ﷺ) ) which nobody knew except him (i.e., Hudhaifa (bin Al-Yaman)). And isn't there among you the person whom Allah gave refuge from Satan through the request (tongue) of Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)? (i.e., `Ammar). Isn't there among you the one who used to carry the Siwak and the cushion (or pillows (of the Prophets)? (i.e., Ibn Mas`ud). How did Ibn Mas`ud use to recite 'By the night as it conceals (the light)?" (Sura 92). 'Alqama said, "Wadhdhakari Wal Untha' (And by male and female.") Abu Ad-Darda added. 'These people continued to argue with me regarding it till they were about to cause me to have doubts although I heard it from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)
hadiths.highlight_arabic: وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ ‏{‏وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
hadiths.highlight_english: These people continued to argue with me regarding it till they were about to cause me to have doubts although I heard it from Allah's Messenger (ﷺ)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء - وأما الجمهور فقرأوا ذلك كما هو مثبت في المصحف الإمام العثماني في سائر الآفاق : ( وما خلق الذكر والأنثى )
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet. However, the majority recited it as it is established in the 'Uthmani Mus-haf in all regions: {By what created the male and the female!}
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: هكذا قرأ ذلك ابن مسعود ، وأبو الدرداء - ورفعه أبو الدرداء
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: This is how Ibn Mas'ud and Abu Ad-Darda' recited it - and Abu Ad-Darda' attributed it to the Prophet.

variants.variant_arabic: وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى
variants.variant_english: By the male and the female!
variants.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا قَبِيصَةُ بْنُ عُقْبَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ عَلْقَمَةَ، قَالَ دَخَلْتُ فِي نَفَرٍ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ الشَّأْمَ فَسَمِعَ بِنَا أَبُو الدَّرْدَاءِ فَأَتَانَا فَقَالَ أَفِيكُمْ مَنْ يَقْرَأُ فَقُلْنَا نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ فَأَيُّكُمْ أَقْرَأُ فَأَشَارُوا إِلَىَّ فَقَالَ اقْرَأْ‏.‏ فَقَرَأْتُ ‏{‏وَاللَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَى * وَالنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّى * وَالذَّكَرِ وَالأُنْثَى‏}‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَنْتَ سَمِعْتَهَا مِنْ فِي صَاحِبِكَ قُلْتُ نَعَمْ‏.‏ قَالَ وَأَنَا سَمِعْتُهَا مِنْ فِي النَّبِيِّ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهَؤُلاَءِ يَأْبَوْنَ عَلَيْنَا‏.‏
variants.hadith_english: Narrated Alqama:I went to Sham with a group of the companions of `Abdullah (bin Mas`ud). Abu Ad-Darda' heard of our arrival so he came to us and said, "Is there anybody among you who can recite (Qur'an)" We replied in the affirmative. Then he asked, "Who is the best reciter?" They pointed at me. Then he told me to recite, so I recited the verse:-- 'By the night as it envelops 'By the day as it appears in brightness; And by the male and the female [wa-l-dhakari wa-l-untha, without 'wa-ma khalaqa'].' (92.1-3) Abu Ad-Darda' then said to me, "Did you hear it (like this) from the mouth of your friend (`Abdullah bin Mas`ud)?" I said, "Yes." He said, "I too, heard it (like this) from the mouth of the Prophet, but these people do not consider this recitation as the correct one

uthmanic_arabic: وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ
uthmanic_english: Did He not find you poor and enrich (you)?

variants.short_title: 93:8 — 'Found You Destitute and Sheltered You'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says 'Did He not find you poor and enrich you?' (ʿā'ilan fa-aghnā), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud read 'find you destitute and shelter you' (ʿadīman fa-āwā).
variants.title: Substitution of 'Destitute and Sheltered' (ʿAdīman Fa-Āwā) in 93:8
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 93:8, the Uthmanic text reads 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَآئِلٗا فَأَغۡنَىٰ' ('Did He not find you poor and enrich (you)?'). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this verse read 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيمًا فَآوَى' ('Did He not find you destitute and shelter (you)?'), replacing both the adjective 'ʿā'ilan' (poor/burdened with dependents) with 'ʿadīman' (destitute) and the rhyme verb 'fa-aghnā' (and enrich) with 'fa-āwā' (and shelter).

variants.variant_target_english: destitute and shelter (you)?

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Commentators view 'ʿadīman' (destitute) as an explanatory synonym for 'ʿā'ilan' (poor) and attribute 'fa-āwā' to an assimilation with the rhyme of verse 93:6 ('Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you [fa-āwā]?').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari explicitly records that 'وَوَجَدَكَ عَدِيمًا فَآوَى' was written in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud (في مصحف عبد الله), representing a two-word consonantal divergence from the Uthmanic text.

variants.short_title: 93:9 — 'Do Not Scowl at the Orphan' (Takhar vs. Taqhar)
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran commands 'As for the orphan, do not oppress him' (fala taqhar, with qāf), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud read 'do not scowl at him' (fala takhar, with kāf).
variants.title: Consonantal Substitution of 'Fa-Lā Takhar' (With Kāf) for 'Fa-Lā Taqhar' in 93:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 93:9, the Uthmanic text commands: 'فَأَمَّا ٱلۡيَتِيمَ فَلَا تَقۡهَرۡ' ('As for the orphan, do not oppress (him),') spelled with the letter qāf. Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this word was written with the letter kāf: 'فَلَا تَكْهَرْ' ('do not scowl at (him),'), from 'kahara' meaning to frown or rebuke harshly.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Linguists and commentators explain 'taqhar' and 'takhar' as closely related phonetic or dialectal forms prohibiting mistreatment or harshness toward orphans.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Because qāf (ق) and kāf (ك) have distinct consonantal skeletons in the Arabic script, 'فَلَا تَكْهَرْ' in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud represents a genuine rasm divergence rather than a diacritical dotting shift.

variants.short_title: 100:9 — Graves 'Excavated' (Buḥitha) vs. 'Ransacked'
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran uses the four-letter verb 'buʿthira' ('when what is in the graves is ransacked'), the Mushaf of Ibn Mas'ud had the three-letter verb 'buḥitha' ('excavated').
variants.title: Triliteral 'Buḥitha' for Quadriliteral 'Buʿthira' in Ibn Mas'ud's Mushaf on 100:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 100:9, the Uthmanic text reads '۞أَفَلَا يَعۡلَمُ إِذَا بُعۡثِرَ مَا فِي ٱلۡقُبُورِ' ('Does he not know? When what is in the graves is ransacked,'). Al-Tabari records that in the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this clause was written 'إِذَا بُحِثَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ' ('When what is in the graves is excavated,'), using the triliteral verb 'buḥitha' (dug up/excavated) without the letter ʿayn or rā' of the quadriliteral 'buʿthira.'

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Lexicographers and commentators explain that 'buʿthira' (overturned/scattered) and 'buḥitha' (dug up/excavated) converge in describing the resurrection of the dead from their graves.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Al-Tabari directly cites the Mushaf of Abdullah bin Mas'ud ('وذكر أنها في مصحف عبد الله: إذا بحث ما في القبور') to establish the lexical meaning of 'buʿthira.'

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وذكر أنها في مصحف عبد الله: " إذا بحث ما في القبور ", وكذلك تأول ذلك أهل التأويل.

uthmanic_arabic: فِي عَمَدٖ مُّمَدَّدَةِۭ
uthmanic_english: in extended columns (of flame).

variants.short_title: 104:9 — Closed Upon Them 'With' vs. 'In' Columns
variants.plain_english_hook: Where the standard Quran says the Fire is closed upon them 'in extended columns' (fī ʿamadin), Abdullah bin Mas'ud's codex read 'with extended columns' (bi-ʿamadin).
variants.title: Reading 'With Extended Columns' (Bi-ʿAmadin) for 'In Extended Columns' in 104:9
variants.diff_summary: In Surah 104:9, the Uthmanic text describes Hellfire as closed over the damned 'فِي عَمَدٖ مُّمَدَّدَةِۭ' ('in extended columns (of flame).'). Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir record via Sufyan al-Thawri from Qatadah that in the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud this verse read 'بِعَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ' ('with extended columns (of flame).'), indicating that the gates of Hell are bolted shut with outstretched pillars rather than the damned being inside columns.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: in extended columns (of flame).
variants.variant_target_english: with extended columns (of flame).
variants.uthmanic_full_arabic: فِي عَمَدٖ مُّمَدَّدَةِۭ

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Grammarians and commentators harmonize the two readings by arguing that the preposition 'fī' (in) in the Uthmanic text can carry the instrumental sense of 'bi-' (with), or that the damned are both inside columns and bolted shut with them.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir cite Ibn Mas'ud's reading 'إِنَّهَا عَلَيْهِمْ مُؤْصَدَةٌ بِعَمَدٍ مُمَدَّدَةٍ' via Qatadah as the primary evidence for the instrumental interpretation.

uthmanic_arabic: تَبَّتۡ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٖ وَتَبَّ
uthmanic_english: The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has perished.

variants.short_title: Addition of 'Qad' ('And He Indeed Perished') in 111:1
variants.plain_english_hook: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4971, Sahih Muslim 208a, and Tafsir al-Tabari, the reading of Abdullah bin Mas'ud and Ibn Abbas adds the particle 'qad' in Surah 111:1 ('wa-qad tabba' instead of 'wa-tabba').
variants.title: Recitation of 'Wa-Qad Tabba' Instead of 'Wa-Tabba' in Surah Al-Masad 111:1
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf ends Surah Al-Masad 111:1 with 'wa-tabba' ('and he has perished'), Sahih al-Bukhari 4971, Sahih Muslim 208a, and Tafsir al-Tabari document the non-Uthmanic reading 'wa-qad tabba' ('and he has indeed perished'), adding the emphatic particle 'qad'. Al-Tabari explicitly identifies this wording as the recitation of Abdullah bin Mas'ud ('fī qirā'ati 'Abdillāh: tabbat yadā Abī Lahabin wa-qad tabba'), while Bukhari and Muslim record its transmission via the Kufan master reciter al-A'mash from Ibn Abbas.
variants.uthmanic_target_english: and he has perished.
variants.variant_target_english: and he has indeed perished.

variants.variant_full_arabic: تَبَّتۡ يَدَآ أَبِي لَهَبٖ وَقَدْ تَبَّ
variants.variant_full_english: The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has indeed perished.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Al-Tabari cites Ibn Mas'ud's reading ('wa-qad tabba') to prove grammatically that the first verb ('tabbat') is a curse ('May the hands of Abu Lahab perish') while the second verb ('wa-tabba') is a declarative statement ('and he has indeed perished').
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Both Sahih al-Bukhari 4971 and Sahih Muslim 208a preserve this reading within the same narrative report as the non-Uthmanic addition in 26:214 ('wa-rahṭaka minhumu al-mukhlaṣīn'), confirming that Kufan reciters transmitted Ibn Mas'ud's consonantal text even after the Uthmanic standardization.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ibn Abbas / Said bin Jubair / Al-Amash
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يُوسُفُ بْنُ مُوسَى، حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، حَدَّثَنَا الأَعْمَشُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَمْرُو بْنُ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ ـ رضى الله عنهما ـ قَالَ لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ ‏{‏وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأَقْرَبِينَ‏}‏ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ، خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى صَعِدَ الصَّفَا فَهَتَفَ ‏"‏ يَا صَبَاحَاهْ ‏"‏‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَنْ هَذَا، فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ‏.‏ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرَأَيْتُمْ إِنْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ سَفْحِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ أَكُنْتُمْ مُصَدِّقِيَّ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالُوا مَا جَرَّبْنَا عَلَيْكَ كَذِبًا‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ ‏"‏‏.‏ قَالَ أَبُو لَهَبٍ تَبًّا لَكَ مَا جَمَعْتَنَا إِلاَّ لِهَذَا ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ‏}‏ وَقَدْ تَبَّ هَكَذَا قَرَأَهَا الأَعْمَشُ يَوْمَئِذٍ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Ibn `Abbas:When the Verse:-- 'And warn your tribe of near kindred.' (26.214) was revealed. Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) went out, and when he had ascended As-Safa mountain, he shouted, "O Sabahah!" The people said, "Who is that?" "Then they gathered around him, whereupon he said, "Do you see? If I inform you that cavalrymen are proceeding up the side of this mountain, will you believe me?" They said, "We have never heard you telling a lie." Then he said, "I am a plain warner to you of a coming severe punishment." Abu Lahab said, "May you perish! You gathered us only for this reason? " Then Abu Lahab went away. So the "Surat:--ul--LAHAB" 'Perish the hands of Abu Lahab!' (111.1) was revealed. {"...and he has perished"} [wa qad tabba]. This is how Al-A'mash recited it on that day.
hadiths.highlight_arabic: ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ ‏{‏تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَتَبَّ‏}‏ وَقَدْ تَبَّ هَكَذَا قَرَأَهَا الأَعْمَشُ يَوْمَئِذٍ
hadiths.highlight_english: {"...and he has perished"} [wa qad tabba]. This is how Al-A'mash recited it on that day.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Ibn Abbas / Said bin Jubair / Al-Amash
hadiths.hadith_arabic: وَحَدَّثَنَا أَبُو كُرَيْبٍ، مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ الْعَلاَءِ حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ، عَنِ الأَعْمَشِ، عَنْ عَمْرِو بْنِ مُرَّةَ، عَنْ سَعِيدِ بْنِ جُبَيْرٍ، عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ، قَالَ لَمَّا نَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ الآيَةُ ‏{‏ وَأَنْذِرْ عَشِيرَتَكَ الأَقْرَبِينَ‏}‏ وَرَهْطَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ ‏.‏ خَرَجَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم حَتَّى صَعِدَ الصَّفَا فَهَتَفَ ‏"‏ يَا صَبَاحَاهْ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ فَقَالُوا مَنْ هَذَا الَّذِي يَهْتِفُ قَالُوا مُحَمَّدٌ ‏.‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي فُلاَنٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ مَنَافٍ يَا بَنِي عَبْدِ الْمُطَّلِبِ ‏"‏ فَاجْتَمَعُوا إِلَيْهِ فَقَالَ ‏"‏ أَرَأَيْتَكُمْ لَوْ أَخْبَرْتُكُمْ أَنَّ خَيْلاً تَخْرُجُ بِسَفْحِ هَذَا الْجَبَلِ أَكُنْتُمْ مُصَدِّقِيَّ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالُوا مَا جَرَّبْنَا عَلَيْكَ كَذِبًا ‏.‏ قَالَ ‏"‏ فَإِنِّي نَذِيرٌ لَكُمْ بَيْنَ يَدَىْ عَذَابٍ شَدِيدٍ ‏"‏ ‏.‏ قَالَ فَقَالَ أَبُو لَهَبٍ تَبًّا لَكَ أَمَا جَمَعْتَنَا إِلاَّ لِهَذَا ثُمَّ قَامَ فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ ‏.‏ كَذَا قَرَأَ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: It is reported on the authority of Ibn 'Abbas that when this verse was revealed:" And warn thy nearest kindred" (and thy group of selected people among them) the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) set off till he climbed Safa' and called loudly: Be on your guard! They said: Who is it calling aloud? They said: Muhammad. They gathered round him, and he said: O sons of so and so, O sons of so and so, O sons of 'Abd Manaf, O sons of 'Abd al-Muttalib, and they gathered around him. He (the Apostle) said: If I were to inform you that there were horsemen emerging out of the foot of this mountain, would you believe me? They said: We have not experienced any lie from you. He said: Well, I am a warner to you before a severe torment. He (the narrator) said that Abu Lahab then said: Destruction to you! Is it for this you have gathered us? He (the Holy Prophet) then stood up, and this verse was revealed:" Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he indeed perished" (cxi. 1). A'mash recited this to the end of the Sura
hadiths.highlight_arabic: فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ السُّورَةُ تَبَّتْ يَدَا أَبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ ‏.‏ كَذَا قَرَأَ الأَعْمَشُ إِلَى آخِرِ السُّورَةِ
hadiths.highlight_english: and this verse was revealed:" Perish the hands of Abu Lahab, and he indeed perished" (cxi. 1). A'mash recited this to the end of the Sura

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وأما قوله: ( وَتَبَّ ) فإنه خبر. ويُذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: " تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ". وفي دخول " قد " فيه دلالة على أنه خبر.
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: As for His saying: {and he has perished}, it is a declarative statement. And it is mentioned that this is in the recitation of 'Abdullāh [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has indeed perished." And in the inclusion of 'qad' (indeed) in it, there is an indication that it is a declarative statement.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: ويُذكر أن ذلك في قراءة عبد الله: " تَبَّتْ يَدَا أبِي لَهَبٍ وَقَدْ تَبَّ"
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: And it is mentioned that this is in the recitation of 'Abdullāh [Ibn Mas'ud]: "The hands of Abū Lahab have perished, and he has indeed perished."

variants.short_title: Ibn Mas'ud's Omission of Surahs 113 and 114
variants.plain_english_hook: Abdullah bin Mas'ud—the first Quran teacher endorsed by Muhammad—omitted the final two chapters (Surahs 113 and 114) from his codex, viewing them as protective prayers rather than chapters of the Book.
variants.title: Exclusion of Al-Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs 113–114) from the Codex of Ibn Mas'ud
variants.diff_summary: Whereas the Uthmanic Mushaf and the codex of Ubayy bin Ka'b include Surah Al-Falaq (113) and Surah An-Nas (114) as the final two chapters of the Quran, Abdullah bin Mas'ud omitted both chapters from his written Mushaf and scraped them out when he saw them written in copies of the text. As documented in Sahih al-Bukhari 4977 and Tafsir Ibn Kathir, Ibn Mas'ud maintained that these two texts were revealed as prophetic invocations for seeking refuge rather than scriptural chapters of the Quranic canon.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical scholars such as Ibn Kathir and al-Nawawi argue that the overwhelming consensus of the Companions—led by Ubayy bin Ka'b—established the Mu'awwidhatayn as canonical chapters, suggesting Ibn Mas'ud initially mistook them for supplications like the Qunut prayer.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: In Sahih al-Bukhari 4977 and multiple chains in Musnad Ahmad and Musnad Abu Ya'la cited by Ibn Kathir, Zirr bin Hubaysh and Alqamah testify that Ibn Mas'ud actively erased the two chapters from his codices and declared, 'They are not from the Book of Allah,' demonstrating that the senior Companions differed over the boundaries of the written canon.

hadiths.transmitted_by: Zirr bin Hubaysh / Ubayy bin Kab
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَلِيُّ بْنُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ، حَدَّثَنَا سُفْيَانُ، حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدَةُ بْنُ أَبِي لُبَابَةَ، عَنْ زِرِّ بْنِ حُبَيْشٍ، وَحَدَّثَنَا عَاصِمٌ، عَنْ زِرٍّ، قَالَ سَأَلْتُ أُبَىَّ بْنَ كَعْبٍ قُلْتُ يَا أَبَا الْمُنْذِرِ إِنَّ أَخَاكَ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا‏.‏ فَقَالَ أُبَىٌّ سَأَلْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم فَقَالَ لِي قِيلَ لِي‏.‏ فَقُلْتُ، قَالَ فَنَحْنُ نَقُولُ كَمَا قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: Narrated Zirr bin Hubaish:I asked Ubai bin Ka`b, "O Abu AlMundhir! Your brother, Ibn Mas`ud said so-and-so (i.e., the two Mu'awwidh-at do not belong to the Qur'an)." Ubai said, "I asked Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) about them, and he said, 'They have been revealed to me, and I have recited them (as a part of the Qur'an)," So Ubai added, "So we say as Allah's Messenger (ﷺ) has said
hadiths.highlight_arabic: إِنَّ أَخَاكَ ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ يَقُولُ كَذَا وَكَذَا
hadiths.highlight_english: Your brother, Ibn Mas`ud said so-and-so (i.e., the two Mu'awwidh-at do not belong to the Qur'an).

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: ورواه عبد الله بن أحمد من حديث الأعمش ، عن أبي إسحاق ، عن عبد الرحمن بن يزيد قال : كان عبد الله يحك المعوذتين من مصاحفه ، ويقول : إنهما ليستا من كتاب الله ... وهذا مشهور عند كثير من القراء والفقهاء : أن ابن مسعود كان لا يكتب المعوذتين في مصحفه .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: 'Abdullah bin Ahmad recorded it from the Hadith of Al-A'mash, from Abu Ishaq, from 'Abdur-Rahman bin Yazid, who said: "'Abdullah used to scrape the Mu'awwidhatayn from his Mushafs, saying: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'" ... This is famous among many of the reciters and jurists, that Ibn Mas'ud did not write the Mu'awwidhatayn in his Mushaf.
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: كان عبد الله يحك المعوذتين من مصاحفه ، ويقول : إنهما ليستا من كتاب الله
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: 'Abdullah used to scrape the Mu'awwidhatayn from his Mushafs, saying: 'They are not from the Book of Allah.'

variants.short_title: Aisha's Testimony on the Lost Suckling Verses
variants.plain_english_hook: Aisha testified in Sahih Muslim that a Quranic verse establishing adult nursing relationships was still actively recited as part of the Quran at the moment Muhammad died, yet it is absent from the Mushaf.
variants.title: The Verses of Ten and Five Sucklings Recited Until the Prophet's Death
variants.diff_summary: In Sahih Muslim 1452a and 1452b, Aisha states that the Quran originally contained a verse stipulating that ten known sucklings establish fosterage prohibition, which was subsequently replaced by five known sucklings. Crucially, Aisha testifies that 'the Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was recited of the Quran' (wa-hunna fīmā yuqra'u min al-Qur'ān), demonstrating that the verse remained in active recitation at the close of prophetic revelation despite its absence from the Uthmanic codex.
variants.variant_target_arabic: عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ يُحَرِّمْنَ ثُمَّ نُسِخْنَ بِخَمْسٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ
variants.variant_target_english: Ten clear sucklings make marriage unlawful, then they were replaced by five clear sucklings
variants.variant_full_arabic: عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ يُحَرِّمْنَ ثُمَّ نُسِخْنَ بِخَمْسٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ
variants.variant_full_english: Ten clear sucklings make marriage unlawful, then they were replaced by five clear sucklings, and the Messenger of Allah died while they were still among what was recited of the Quran.

scholarly_discussion.classical_harmonization: Classical commentators such as al-Nawawi suggest that the abrogation of the five-suckling recitation occurred very close to the Prophet's death, so those who had not yet heard of its cancellation continued reciting it briefly.
scholarly_discussion.primary_source_evaluation: Because divine revelation and abrogation necessarily ceased at the moment of the Prophet's death, Aisha's explicit testimony in Sahih Muslim 1452a that the verse was still recited when he died—combined with her continued enforcement of the five-suckling legal ruling—poses a direct challenge to post-prophetic abrogation claims.

hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا يَحْيَى بْنُ يَحْيَى، قَالَ قَرَأْتُ عَلَى مَالِكٍ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ أَبِي بَكْرٍ، عَنْ عَمْرَةَ، عَنْ عَائِشَةَ، أَنَّهَا قَالَتْ كَانَ فِيمَا أُنْزِلَ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ يُحَرِّمْنَ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ نُسِخْنَ بِخَمْسٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english: A'isha (Allah be pleased with her) reported that it had been revealed in the Holy Qur'an that ten clear sucklings make the marriage unlawful, then it was abrogated (and substituted) by five sucklings and Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) died and it was before that time (found) in the Holy Qur'an (and recited by the Muslims)
hadiths.highlight_arabic: عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ يُحَرِّمْنَ ‏.‏ ثُمَّ نُسِخْنَ بِخَمْسٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ فَتُوُفِّيَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صلى الله عليه وسلم وَهُنَّ فِيمَا يُقْرَأُ مِنَ الْقُرْآنِ
hadiths.highlight_english: ten clear sucklings make the marriage unlawful, then it was abrogated (and substituted) by five sucklings and Allah's Apostle (ﷺ) died and it was before that time (found) in the Holy Qur'an

hadiths.transmitted_by: Amrah bint Abdur-Rahman / Yahya bin Said
hadiths.hadith_arabic: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ مَسْلَمَةَ الْقَعْنَبِيُّ، حَدَّثَنَا سُلَيْمَانُ بْنُ بِلاَلٍ، عَنْ يَحْيَى، - وَهُوَ ابْنُ سَعِيدٍ - عَنْ عَمْرَةَ، أَنَّهَا سَمِعَتْ عَائِشَةَ، تَقُولُ - وَهْىَ تَذْكُرُ الَّذِي يُحَرِّمُ مِنَ الرَّضَاعَةِ - قَالَتْ عَمْرَةُ فَقَالَتْ عَائِشَةُ نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ أَيْضًا خَمْسٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ ‏.‏
hadiths.hadith_english:
Amra reported that she heard 'A'isha (Allah he pleased with her) discussing fosterage which (makes marriage) unlawful; and she ('A'isha) said:
There was revealed in the Holy Qur'an ten clear sucklings, and then five clear (sucklings)
hadiths.highlight_arabic: نَزَلَ فِي الْقُرْآنِ عَشْرُ رَضَعَاتٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ ثُمَّ نَزَلَ أَيْضًا خَمْسٌ مَعْلُومَاتٌ
hadiths.highlight_english: There was revealed in the Holy Qur'an ten clear sucklings, and then five clear (sucklings)

tafsir_sources.arabic_excerpt: وقال آخرون : لا يحرم أقل من خمس رضعات ، لما ثبت في صحيح مسلم من طريق مالك ، عن عبد الله بن أبي بكر ، عن عمرة عن عائشة ، رضي الله عنها ، قالت : كان فيما أنزل [ الله ] من القرآن : عشر رضعات معلومات يحرمن . ثم نسخن بخمس معلومات ، فتوفي رسول الله صلى لله عليه وسلم وهن فيما يقرأ من القرآن .
tafsir_sources.english_excerpt: Others said: Less than five sucklings do not prohibit, based on what is established in Sahih Muslim by way of Malik, from Abdullah bin Abi Bakr, from Amrah, from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: "Among what Allah revealed of the Quran was: 'Ten known sucklings prohibit.' Then they were abrogated by 'five known sucklings.' The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died while they were still among what was recited of the Quran."
tafsir_sources.highlight_arabic: فتوفي رسول الله صلى لله عليه وسلم وهن فيما يقرأ من القرآن
tafsir_sources.highlight_english: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) died while they were still among what was recited of the Quran.
